cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese minimum 50%, Cabernet Franc and/or Cabernet Sauvignon 10 to 20%, Canaiolo up to 20%. DOC 1975; DOCG 1990.

cards.q: Find Chianti. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese (minimum 60%; 75% in the Colli Senesi), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds (Cabernet up to 15%) and up to 10% white grapes; a rosato was added in 2026. DOC 1967; DOCG 1984 (subzone Terre di Vinci 2026).

cards.q: Find Chianti Classico. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese (minimum 80%; 90% for Gran Selezione from 2027), with Canaiolo, Colorino, Malvasia Nera, Ciliegiolo and, outside Gran Selezione, some international reds. DOC 1967 (as Chianti subzone); separate DOCG 1996.

cards.q: Find Elba Aleatico Passito. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. 100% Aleatico. DOC 1967 (within Elba); DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Montecucco Sangiovese. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese minimum 90%. Montecucco DOC 1998; DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Morellino di Scansano. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese (locally Morellino) minimum 85%. DOC 1978; DOCG 2006.

cards.q: Find Suvereto. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot (blends or varietal), Sangiovese. Subzone of Val di Cornia 1989; separate DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Val di Cornia Rosso. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Vernaccia di San Gimignano. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Vernaccia di San Gimignano minimum 85%; up to 10% Riesling and/or Sauvignon Blanc. DOC 1966 (first Italian DOC); DOCG 1993.

cards.q: Find Vino Nobile di Montepulciano. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Tuscany. Sangiovese (locally Prugnolo Gentile) minimum 70%; Pieve tier minimum 85% with only native partners. DOC 1966; DOCG 1980; Pieve UGAs approved 2023, in force from the 2021 vintage.

cards.q: Find Montefalco Sagrantino. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Umbria. 100% Sagrantino. DOC 1979 (within Montefalco); DOCG 1992; renamed 2009.

cards.q: Find Torgiano Rosso Riserva. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Umbria. Sangiovese 70% or more, with Canaiolo and other reds. DOC 1968; Riserva DOCG 1990.

cards.q: Find Amarone della Valpolicella. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Corvina and Corvinone (45 to 95%), Rondinella (5 to 30%), plus up to 25% other local reds such as Molinara and Oseleta. DOC 1990, DOCG 2010.

cards.q: Find Bagnoli Friularo. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Raboso Piave (Friularo) min 90%. DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Bardolino Superiore. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Corvina (35 to 80%), Rondinella. DOCG 2001.

cards.q: Find Colli Asolani - Prosecco. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Glera (min 85%). DOCG 2009.

cards.q: Find Colli di Conegliano. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Cabernet, Merlot, Marzemino; Manzoni Bianco, Pinot Bianco; Verdiso; Torchiato di Fregona. DOC 1993, DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Colli Euganei Fior d'Arancio. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Moscato Giallo (min 95%). DOCG 2010.

cards.q: Find Conegliano Valdobbiadene - Prosecco. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Glera (min 85%), Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera, Glera lunga. DOC 1969, DOCG 2009.

cards.q: Find Lison. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Friulano (Tai) min 85%. DOCG 2010.

cards.q: Find Montello Rosso. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Carmenère. DOCG 2011.

cards.q: Find Piave Malanotte. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Raboso Piave (min 70%). DOCG 2010.

cards.q: Find Recioto della Valpolicella. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella (same as Amarone). DOC 1968, DOCG 2010.

cards.q: Find Recioto di Gambellara. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Garganega (100%). DOCG 2008.

cards.q: Find Recioto di Soave. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Garganega (min 70%). DOCG 1998.

cards.q: Find Soave Superiore. Region, grapes and status history?
cards.a: Veneto. Garganega (min 70%), Trebbiano di Soave. DOCG 2001.

cards.q: How many DOCGs did Italy have at the end of 2025?
cards.a: 78, plus just over 330 DOCs (CSW 2026 addendum). The newest include Casauria (Abruzzo) and Cirò Classico, Calabria's first DOCG (2025).

cards.q: Which were the first four DOCGs (1980)?
cards.a: Barolo, Barbaresco, Brunello di Montalcino and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano; Albana di Romagna (1987) was the first white.

cards.q: Which regions have only one DOCG?
cards.a: Sardinia (Vermentino di Gallura), Sicily (Cerasuolo di Vittoria) and Calabria (Cirò Classico, 2025); Basilicata's only DOCG is Aglianico del Vulture Superiore.

cards.q: When was Italy's DOC law passed, and what was the first DOC?
cards.a: Law 930 of 12 July 1963; Vernaccia di San Gimignano became the first DOC in 1966.

decks.title: Barolo: communes and MGAs
decks.description: Key Menzioni Geografiche Aggiuntive of Barolo and the commune each sits in.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cannubi. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. The most famous name in Barolo and the first to appear on a label: a bottle marked 'Cannubi 1752' is said to survive.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cannubi Boschis. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. The north-eastern, east-facing end of the Cannubi hill above the road to Alba.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cannubi San Lorenzo. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. The southern slope of the Cannubi hill closest to Barolo village.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cannubi Valletta. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. The western flank of the Cannubi hill, facing south-west into the little valley (valletta) that separates Cannubi from Sarmassa. Slightly cooler and more sheltered than the core, it gives fragrant, fine-tannined wines.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cannubi Muscatel. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. The south-western tip of the Cannubi hill above the hamlet of Muscatel, named for the Moscato once grown here. It is the smallest and least known of the Cannubi family, on sandier soils near the village.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Sarmassa. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. A spur between Brunate and Cannubi on the Barolo side of the La Morra border.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Le Coste. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. Steep, south-facing slopes just south-west of Barolo village on the road toward Vergne. Giuseppe Rinaldi's 'Brunate-Le Coste' blend was split when the MGA rules forbade double names; Le Coste now goes into his Tre Tine and Bussia.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Castellero. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. A small, south-west-facing slope east of Barolo village toward the Castiglione Falletto border. Giacomo Brezza and the Barale family make classic, medium-weight Castellero from old vines.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Terlo. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. South-east of Barolo village toward Monforte and Novello, bordering Ravera. Higher and cooler than Cannubi, it gives tight, mineral wines that have gained favour in warm vintages.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Paiagallo. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. A steep south-facing slope just below Barolo village on the south. Its name means 'rooster's straw' in dialect.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Coste di Rose. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. A high ridge between Barolo and Monforte with sandy, almost white soils. Coste di Rose wines are pale, perfumed and graceful, a showcase for the sandy end of Barolo's spectrum.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco delle Viole. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. The highest point of the Barolo commune, around 450 to 480 m near the chapel of San Pietro delle Viole above the hamlet of Vergne. G.D.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Liste. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. A south-facing amphitheatre west of Barolo village below Vergne. Borgogno, the old Barolo house founded in 1761 and revived by the Farinetti family, has made Liste its flagship single vineyard.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Fossati. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo and La Morra. Straddling the Barolo and La Morra border north-west of Barolo village, Fossati faces south-east and gives perfumed, mid-weight Barolo. Enzo Boglietti and Dosio bottle it.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Rué. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barolo. A small site between Barolo village and Cannubi, one of the four parcels in Bartolo Mascarello's classic blend. Today Rué is bottled on its own by a few growers.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Brunate. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra and Barolo. One of the two or three greatest crus of the western Barolo zone, about 25 ha on a steep south to south-east-facing slope below the little Brunate chapel, straddling the La Morra and Barolo border.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cerequio. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra and Barolo. A natural amphitheatre just west of Brunate, around the restored hamlet of Palais Cerequio.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Rocche dell'Annunziata. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. About 30 ha of steep, crumbling slopes (rocche) dropping from the hamlet of Torriglione toward the Annunziata valley. Two sectors, one facing south-east and one south to south-west, on blue marl veined with sand.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Arborina. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. A gentle, south-east-facing slope north of the Annunziata.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Gattera. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. North-east of the Annunziata, where Mauro Veglio and Bovio farm. Gattera wines are generous and early to open.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Conca. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. A tiny, south-facing amphitheatre (conca means bowl) just below Ratti's Abbazia dell'Annunziata. Renato Ratti's Conca was one of the first single-vineyard Barolos of the 1970s.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Serradenari. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. The highest MGA in La Morra, around 500 to 530 m on the ridge south-west of the village. Once thought too cool for Barolo, it now makes taut, fragrant wines prized in hot years.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Case Nere. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. On the La Morra side of the Barolo border near Fossati, south-facing. Enzo Boglietti's Case Nere is the best known.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco San Biagio. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. A hilltop site east of Santa Maria named after its chapel, giving supple, fragrant wines.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco Manzoni. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: La Morra. Not to be confused with Rocche dei Manzoni in Monforte: a small rise near the hamlet of Manzoni at the eastern edge of La Morra, toward the Castiglione Falletto border.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Monprivato. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. About 7 ha on the south-west-facing slope below Castiglione Falletto, almost entirely owned by Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Villero. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. A large south-west-facing amphitheatre south of Castiglione village with deep marl, considered by many the finest site in the commune.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Rocche di Castiglione. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto and Monforte d'Alba. A narrow escarpment running south from Castiglione Falletto toward Perno, facing south-east above the valley toward Serralunga. The steep, crumbling sandstone and marl give the most elegant, aromatic wines of the commune.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco Boschis. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. The hill north-east of Castiglione Falletto that is essentially the Cavallotto family estate, which they have farmed since 1928 and bottled since 1948. Vigna San Giuseppe, the steep heart, gives their famous Riserva.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Fiasco. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. A west-facing slope near Paolo Scavino's winery; Scavino's 'Bric del Fiasc' from here made Enrico Scavino's reputation as a modernist in the 1980s.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Mariondino. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. South-west of the village toward Bussia, giving fine, mid-weight wines. Parusso and Armando Parusso farm here.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Scarrone. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. Directly below Vietti's cellar in the village, famous for Vietti's old-vine Barbera d'Alba Vigna Scarrone and Vigna Vecchia Scarrone as much as for Nebbiolo.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Pira. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. North-west of the village; Roagna's Pira estate, bought in 1989, is a monument of traditional winemaking with very long macerations.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco Rocche. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. The top of the Castiglione hill above the Rocche, a Ceretto monopole crowned by their glass tasting cube. Ceretto's Bricco Rocche was one of the first prestige single-vineyard Barolos of the 1980s.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Montanello. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Castiglione Falletto. A south-west-facing slope on the road from Castiglione to Monforte, named after the Tenuta Montanello whose 18th-century cellar still stands.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bussia. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba and Barolo. With almost 300 ha, the largest MGA in Barolo and the clearest case of how an MGA is a place name, not a quality rank. It sweeps from the Barolo border through a series of amphitheatres toward Castiglione Falletto.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Ginestra. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. A broad, south to south-east-facing amphitheatre east of Monforte village at 300 to 450 m, on compact Serravallian sandstone and marl. Ginestra wines are deep, dark and long-lived.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Mosconi. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. South of Ginestra near Case Mosconi, rising to about 450 m. Long split among small growers, it became sought-after when Pio Cesare and Conterno Fantino bought in, and is known for broad, structured wines.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Castelletto. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. Near the hamlet of Castelletto by Perno, facing east to south-east toward Serralunga. Fortemasso and Giuseppe Mascarello hold vines here.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Gramolere. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. A west-facing slope around Cascina Gramolere between Bussia and Castelletto; Giovanni Manzone's Gramolere is the benchmark.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Santo Stefano di Perno. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. Slopes around the hamlet of Perno facing east toward Serralunga. Giuseppe Mascarello's Santo Stefano di Perno is the reference, a firmer, more austere counterpart to his Monprivato.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Le Coste di Monforte. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. South-east of Monforte village on high, sandy slopes. Often finer and more floral than the rest of Monforte.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco San Pietro. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Monforte d'Alba. A large, high MGA west of Monforte by Bussia San Pietro, rising above 500 m. Increasingly valued for freshness in hot vintages.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Francia. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. Giacomo Conterno's 14-ha monopole, bought by Giovanni Conterno in 1974 from the estate of Cascina Francia. The source of Monfortino (since the 1978 vintage) and of Barolo Cascina Francia, now labelled simply 'Francia'.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Arione. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. The southernmost great vineyard of Serralunga, next to Francia. Roberto Conterno bought most of it from the Gigi Rosso family in 2015, releasing Barolo Arione from 2015; the purchase was the headline land deal of that decade.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Falletto. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. Bruno Giacosa's estate vineyard, bought in 1982, south of Serralunga village. The upper sector gives Le Rocche del Falletto, whose Riserva (red label) is among the most coveted Barolos made.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Vignarionda. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. About 10 ha of south to south-west-facing amphitheatre at around 330 m south of Serralunga village, on calcareous marl.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Lazzarito. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. An elevated, sheltered site south-east of the village with marked limestone. Its name may come from a lazaretto (plague hospital).

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Ornato. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. Around the hamlet of Ornato south of the village, south-west facing. Pio Cesare's Ornato, first released in 1985, made it famous.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Cerretta. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. A long ridge in the north of Serralunga around the hamlet of Cerretta, at 300 to 400 m. Ettore Germano, Giovanni Rosso and Elio Altare (who bought in 2007) make powerful, tannic Cerretta.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Parafada. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. A west-facing slope north of the village around Cascina Parafada, giving rich, ripe Serralunga. Massolino's Parafada is the reference.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Badarina. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. A high, south-east-facing site in the south-east of the commune toward Roddino. Bruna Grimaldi's Badarina is the best-known bottling.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Briccolina. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. A small, steep slope near Francia in the south of Serralunga, known through Batasiolo's single-vineyard bottling.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Gabutti. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. Just east of the village, a site associated with the Cappellano family's Pie Franco and Pie Rupestris bottlings (from ungrafted and grafted vines) and with Gabutti-Boasso.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Prapò. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. A steep, south-east-facing amphitheatre in the north-east of Serralunga. Ceretto, Ettore Germano and Schiavenza bottle it.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Marenca. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. Just north-west of the village, adjoining Margheria; Luigi Pira's Marenca is the classic.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Margheria. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. West-facing, just below Serralunga's castle, sandier and gentler than most of the commune. Massolino and Luigi Pira bottle it.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Baudana. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. In the north of Serralunga around the hamlet of Baudana, with mixed exposures. Luigi Baudana's small estate, now owned by G.D.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Boscareto. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. South-east of the village on high ground; Batasiolo and Ferdinando Principiano bottle it.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Fontanafredda. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba. The royal hunting estate given by King Vittorio Emanuele II to his mistress Rosa Vercellana, 'la Bela Rosin', in 1858; their son Emanuele Alberto began making wine here in 1878.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Sorano. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Serralunga d'Alba and Diano d'Alba. A small MGA by the hamlet of Sorano that crosses into Diano d'Alba, one of the few Barolo crus shared with Diano.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Monvigliero. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Verduno. The grand cru of Verduno: a south-facing slope east of the village, on the Tanaro side of the zone, with sandy Tortonian marl. Its wines are perfumed, spicy and transparent, with famous whole-cluster interpretations by G.B.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Massara. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Verduno. South-west of Verduno toward La Morra; Castello di Verduno's Massara is the main bottling.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Breri. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Verduno. A slope by the hamlet of Breri east of Verduno, close to Roddi.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Ravera. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Novello and Barolo. A high ridge east of Novello at 380 to 450 m, bordering Barolo's Terlo. Elvio Cogno's estate sits on it, and Vietti's Ravera (first vintage 2008) quickly became one of their top wines.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Panerole. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Novello. Below the hamlet of Panerole east of Novello, a high, fresh site.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Castello. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Grinzane Cavour. The vineyard below the castle of Grinzane Cavour, where Cavour managed the family estate and, with the help of Paolo Francesco Staglieno, made some of the first dry, cellar-aged Barolo in the 1830s and 1840s.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Garretti. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Grinzane Cavour. On the western edge of Grinzane toward Gallo d'Alba; one of the lower, warmer MGAs of the zone.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Bricco Ambrogio. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Roddi. The only MGA in Roddi, a south-facing hill above the Tanaro near the castle. Paolo Scavino's Bricco Ambrogio showed what Roddi could do.

cards.q: Find the Barolo MGA Mantoetto. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Cherasco. The only MGA in Cherasco, the westernmost and smallest outpost of Barolo, near the confluence of the Tanaro and Stura.

cards.q: How many communes may make Barolo, and which five make most of it?
cards.a: Eleven: Barolo, La Morra, Castiglione Falletto, Serralunga d'Alba and Monforte d'Alba (the core five), plus Novello, Verduno, Grinzane Cavour, Diano d'Alba, Cherasco and Roddi (parts).

cards.q: How many MGAs does Barolo have, and when were they introduced?
cards.a: 181 Menzioni Geografiche Aggiuntive, from the 2010 vintage (Italian Wine Central figure), including 11 village MGAs.

cards.q: Which soils divide the Barolo zone?
cards.a: Tortonian marls in the west (La Morra, Barolo): softer, perfumed wines. Serravallian (Helvetian) sandstone and marl in the east (Serralunga, Monforte, Castiglione Falletto): more power and tannin.

cards.q: Barolo minimum ageing, normale and riserva?
cards.a: 38 months (18 in wood) and 62 months (18 in wood), counted from 1 November of the harvest year; min 13% abv.

cards.q: Why is Cannubi famous?
cards.a: The most celebrated MGA of Barolo village, on the oldest recorded label ("Cannubi 1752"); its sub-zones (Boschis, San Lorenzo, Valletta, Muscatel) may add Cannubi to their names.

decks.title: Barbaresco: communes and MGAs
decks.description: Barbaresco, Neive and Treiso crus.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Asili. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. About 14 ha of south-west-facing slope at 200 to 270 m south of Barbaresco village, on silty loam, clay and sand over marl. Asili is the most perfumed of the great Barbaresco crus, all violets and silk.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Rabajà. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. About 20 ha facing south and south-west south of Asili and Martinenga, on limestone with sand and clay. Rabajà gives a fuller, more muscular Barbaresco than Asili, with black cherry and spice.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Martinenga. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. A 12-ha amphitheatre between Asili and Rabajà, a monopole of the Marchesi di Grésy since the 18th century. Its two best parcels, Camp Gros and Gaiun, are bottled as Riservas.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Montestefano. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. A steep, south-facing slope east of the village with high calcium content, giving the most structured and tannic wines of Barbaresco.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Montefico. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. North-east of the village, adjoining Montestefano, on white calcareous marl. Tight and mineral; Roagna's Montefico Vecchie Viti and the Produttori Riserva are benchmarks.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Ovello. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. North-west of the village above the Tanaro, cooler and later-ripening. Produttori del Barbaresco and Cantina del Pino make classic Ovello.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Pora. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. West of Asili, south-west facing, a lighter, fragrant style. Produttori bottles a Pora Riserva and Ca' del Baio a Pora.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Rio Sordo. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. West of Rabajà on the slope down to the 'silent stream' (rio sordo) toward Treiso, with sandier soils. Produttori, Cascina Bruciata and Brovia bottle it.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Pajè. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. Just south-west of the village. Roagna's Pajè is one of the great old-school Barbarescos, and Produttori makes a Pajè Riserva.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Moccagatta. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. North of Asili around the hamlet and winery of the same name. Produttori del Barbaresco's Moccagatta Riserva and the Minuto family's Moccagatta estate.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Secondine. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. Between the village and Asili, the source of Gaja's Sorì San Lorenzo, a south-facing parcel the Gajas bought in 1964 that took its name from the patron saint of Alba's cathedral, which once owned it.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Roncaglie. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. West of the village toward the Tanaro, home of Gaja's Sorì Tildin, named after Angelo Gaja's grandmother Clotilde Rey.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Faset. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. North of the village, sloping toward the Tanaro; Bottega and Castello di Verduno farm here.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Tre Stelle. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Barbaresco. Around the hamlet of Tre Stelle in the south of the commune; Sottimano's and Rizzi's parcels nearby.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Gallina. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. A south-facing hill west of Neive village that gives rich, ripe wines; La Spinetta's Gallina, Ugo Lequio and Oddero's Gallina are the best known.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Albesani. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. A large MGA north-west of Neive, south-facing. It contains the vineyard of Santo Stefano, made famous by Bruno Giacosa and owned by Castello di Neive, as well as Cantina del Pino and Piero Busso holdings.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Starderi. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. North of Neive around the hamlet of Starderi, the source of La Spinetta's Starderi.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Serraboella. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. East of Neive near Bricco di Neive; Cigliuti and Paitin (whose Sorì Paitin is here) are the reference estates.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Cottà. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. On the Neive side of the border with Barbaresco, near the hamlet of Cottà, south-west facing. Sottimano's Cottà is the classic.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Currà. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. A small, steep, south-west-facing site in Neive near the Barbaresco border, next to Gallina, on sandy marl. Sottimano and Bruno Rocca bottle Currà as an intense, spicy single-vineyard Barbaresco.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Basarin. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. South of Neive on high ground; Adriano Marco e Vittorio and Moccagatta bottle it.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Bricco di Neive. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Neive. The high hill east of Neive at around 400 m, one of the coolest spots in the zone.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Pajorè. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Treiso. Treiso's most historic cru, on the border with Barbaresco, famed in the 19th century. Sottimano and Rizzi have restored its reputation; Gaja's Sorì Tildin and the Giacosa family once bought grapes here.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Marcarini. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Treiso. Around the hamlet of Marcarini near Ferrere, home of Ca' del Baio and of Ada Nada's vines.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Nervo. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Treiso. A high west-facing slope in Treiso toward San Rocco Seno d'Elvio, known for fresh, sinewy wines.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Rizzi. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Treiso. The MGA around the Dellapiana family's Rizzi estate, a source of lean, perfumed Treiso Barbaresco.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Pertinace. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Treiso. Named after the hamlet of Pertinace, birthplace (by tradition) of the Roman emperor Publius Helvius Pertinax (reigned AD 193). Home of the Cantina Vignaioli Elvio Pertinace cooperative.

cards.q: Find the Barbaresco MGA Meruzzano. Which commune, and what is it like?
cards.a: Treiso. The southernmost part of the Barbaresco zone around the hamlet of Meruzzano, high and cool at up to 450 m.

cards.q: Which communes make Barbaresco?
cards.a: Barbaresco, Neive and Treiso, plus San Rocco Seno d'Elvio (part of Alba).

cards.q: How many MGAs does Barbaresco have?
Barbaresco minimum ageing, normale and riserva?
cards.a: 26 months (9 in wood) and 50 months (9 in wood), from 1 November of the harvest year; min 12.5% abv.

cards.q: Find Asili. Why is it famous?
cards.a: A Barbaresco village MGA prized by Bruno Giacosa, Ceretto and the Produttori del Barbaresco: perfumed, fine-tannined.

decks.title: Tuscany: DOCGs, Chianti subzones and Chianti Classico UGAs
decks.description: The 11 UGAs, the Chianti subzones and the rules of the great Tuscan DOCGs.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Castellina.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. One of the three founding members of the medieval Lega del Chianti, Castellina sits on the ridge that splits the Pesa and Elsa valleys.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Castelnuovo Berardenga.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. The southernmost and warmest UGA, where Chianti Classico runs down toward the clay hills of the Crete Senesi.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Gaiole.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. Gaiole spreads across the eastern Monti del Chianti, a high, wooded commune that includes Brolio, Coltibuono, Ama and Rietine.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Greve.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. The Greve UGA is the northern and eastern part of the commune once Panzano, and from 2027 Lamole and Montefioralle, are carved out.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Lamole.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. A tiny hamlet of terraces high above Greve (roughly 500 to 650 m), with dry-stone walls rebuilt by hand and sandstone soils (macigno) that give pale, high-toned, floral Sangiovese.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Montefioralle.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. A walled medieval village on the hill just west of Greve, believed to be the family home of Amerigo Vespucci.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Panzano.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. Panzano is the frazione in the southwest of Greve commune famous for the Conca d'Oro, a south-facing amphitheatre of galestro and alberese that collects heat and gives some of the most complete Sangiovese in Tuscany.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Radda.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. Radda was the capital of the Lega del Chianti and is now the reference for high-altitude, galestro-driven Sangiovese: pale, perfumed and nervy, sometimes austere in youth.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA San Casciano.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. The northern gateway to the zone, on lower, gentler hills toward Florence, with sandstone and Pliocene sands.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA San Donato in Poggio.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. This UGA joins the western half of Barberino Tavarnelle with the northern tip of Poggibonsi, centred on the walled village of San Donato.

cards.q: Find the Chianti Classico UGA Vagliagli.
cards.a: One of the 11 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, approved by the consortium in 2021 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 1 July 2023; usable on Gran Selezione labels. A hamlet in western Castelnuovo Berardenga, higher and cooler than the southern part of the commune, with alberese and sandstone.

cards.q: Find Chianti Colli Aretini.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone defined 1932.

cards.q: Find Chianti Colli Fiorentini.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone defined 1932.

cards.q: Find Chianti Colli Senesi.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone defined 1932.

cards.q: Find Chianti Colline Pisane.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone defined 1932.

cards.q: Find Chianti Montalbano.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone defined 1932.

cards.q: Find Chianti Montespertoli.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone 1996.

cards.q: Find Chianti Rùfina.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone defined 1932.

cards.q: Find Chianti Terre di Vinci.
cards.a: A subzone of the wider Chianti DOCG, not Chianti Classico. Subzone 2026.

cards.q: Find Chianti Classico. Its quality pyramid?
cards.a: Annata, Riserva and Gran Selezione (since 2014); min 80% Sangiovese; Gran Selezione min 90% Sangiovese from the 2027 vintage with only native grapes for the rest; black rooster (Gallo Nero) seal.

cards.q: When was Chianti first delimited?
cards.a: 24 September 1716, by Grand Duke Cosimo III de' Medici, who also named Carmignano, Pomino and Val d'Arno di Sopra.

cards.q: What separates Chianti DOCG from Chianti Classico DOCG?
cards.a: Chianti is a larger, separate DOCG with seven historic subzones plus Terre di Vinci; Classico is the historic core between Florence and Siena, its own DOCG since 1996.

cards.q: Brunello di Montalcino rules?
cards.a: 100% Sangiovese; released 1 January of the fifth year after harvest (sixth for riserva), with at least 2 years in oak; DOCG 1980.

cards.q: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano: grape and recent change?
cards.a: Min 70% Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile); Pieve sub-areas approved in 2023 for the top wines.

cards.q: Find Bolgheri. Which DOC sub-appellation is a single estate?
cards.a: Bolgheri Sassicaia, the first single-estate DOC in Italy (1994).

cards.q: What is galestro?
cards.a: A friable, schistous clay-marl of Chianti Classico (Radda, Gaiole) and northern Montalcino; gives perfume and finesse.

cards.q: What is alberese?
cards.a: A hard, pale limestone of Chianti Classico (Castellina, Panzano); gives structure and depth.

decks.title: Spain: DOCa, DOQ and Vinos de Pago
decks.description: Rioja and Priorat, the Vinos de Pago estates and Spain's quality tiers.

cards.q: Find Rioja. Status and year?
cards.a: DOCa (Denominación de Origen Calificada) since 1991, the first in Spain; DO statute 1925 (Consejo), 1932 law.

cards.q: Find Rioja Alta.
cards.a: Western, higher and cooler sub-zone south of the Ebro; clay-limestone and alluvial soils; classic long-lived Tempranillo (Haro, Cenicero).

cards.q: Find Rioja Alavesa.
cards.a: In the Basque province of Álava, north of the Ebro below the Sierra de Cantabria; chalky clay, finer Tempranillo (Laguardia).

cards.q: Find Rioja Oriental.
cards.a: The warmer, drier eastern sub-zone (formerly Rioja Baja), more Garnacha.

cards.q: Find Priorat. Status, soil and grapes?
cards.a: DOQ (Catalan for DOCa) since 2000 regionally and 2009 nationally; llicorella slate; Garnatxa and Samsó (Cariñena).

cards.q: Find L'Ermita. Its classification?
cards.a: Gran Vinya Classificada of Priorat (Álvaro Palacios, Gratallops); old Garnatxa on north-east-facing llicorella.

cards.q: What is a Vi de Vila?
cards.a: A Priorat village wine from one of its 12 villages (here Gratallops); the pyramid runs Vi de Finca and Gran Vinya Classificada above.

cards.q: Rioja red ageing rules: Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva?
cards.a: Crianza 2 years with at least 1 in oak; Reserva 3 years with at least 1 in oak; Gran Reserva 5 years with at least 2 in oak and 2 in bottle (Rioja rule, stricter than national).

cards.q: What is Viñedo Singular in Rioja?
cards.a: A single-vineyard category (2017): vines at least 35 years old, low yields, hand harvest; also vino de zona and vino de municipio labels.

cards.q: Why did Rioja boom in the 1870s?
cards.a: Phylloxera in France drove Bordeaux merchants to Rioja for wine; they brought barrel ageing, and the railway to Haro carried it north.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Chozas Carrascal. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Valencia; recognised 2020 (EU). Grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet, Syrah, Monastrell; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Macabeo.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Los Balagueses. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Valencia; recognised 2011. Grapes: Syrah, Merlot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Dehesa del Carrizal. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2006 (EU register 2009). Grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Vallegarcía. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2019. Grapes: Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot; Viognier.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Finca Élez. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2002 (regional); EU register 2009. Grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Guijoso. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2004 (EU register 2007). Grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Casa del Blanco. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2010 (EU register 2011). Grapes: Cabernet, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Los Cerrillos. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2019. Grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Calzadilla. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2011. Grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Pago Florentino. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2009. Grapes: Tempranillo (Cencibel), Syrah, Petit Verdot.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago El Vicario. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2019. Grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Graciano, Garnacha; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago El Terrerazo. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Valencia; recognised date not documented. Grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Vera de Estenas. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Valencia; recognised 2019. Grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Campo de La Guardia. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2009. Grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Malbec; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago La Jaraba. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2019. Grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Graciano; Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Dominio de Valdepusa. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2003. Grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Graciano.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Pago de Otazu. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Navarra; recognised 2008. Grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Aylés. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Aragón; recognised 2010 (national); EU 2011. Grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Dehesa Peñalba. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla y León; recognised 2022. Grapes: Tempranillo, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Urueña. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla y León; recognised 2021. Grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Pago de Arínzano. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Navarra; recognised 2007. Grapes: Tempranillo, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon; Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Prado de Irache. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Navarra; recognised 2008. Grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuela, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Abadía Retuerta. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla y León; recognised 2022. Grapes: Tempranillo (about three-quarters), Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Merlot; whites from Albillo Mayor, Sauvignon Blanc, Godello, Verdejo.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Bolandin. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Navarra; recognised 2020s. Grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Urbezo. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Aragón; recognised 2024. Grapes: Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon, Mazuela, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Garnacha Blanca, Moscatel de Alejandría.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Río Negro. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2025. Grapes: Tempranillo, Tinto Fragoso, Syrah, Cabernet, Merlot; Gewürztraminer.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Rosalejo. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Castilla-La Mancha; recognised 2024. Grapes: Varieties not documented in the sources consulted.

cards.q: Find the Vino de Pago Tharsys. Region and recognition?
cards.a: Valencia; recognised 2025. Grapes: Bobal and other reds; whites and sparkling.

cards.q: Which was the first Vino de Pago?
cards.a: Dominio de Valdepusa (Marqués de Griñón, Toledo), 2003, with Finca Élez.

cards.q: What is a Vino de Pago?
cards.a: Spain's single-estate PDO tier: a property with its own terroir and reputation, wine made and bottled by the estate; most are in Castilla-La Mancha, Navarra and Valencia.

decks.title: Sherry: pagos and styles
decks.description: The albariza pagos and the biological and oxidative styles.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Macharnudo. Which town?
cards.a: Jerez de la Frontera. The most famous Sherry pago, a range of albariza hills north of Jerez rising to about 135 m.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Carrascal. Which town?
cards.a: Jerez de la Frontera. A pago of albariza hills just north of Jerez, beside Macharnudo, known for powerful olorosos and amontillados.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Balbaína. Which town?
cards.a: Jerez de la Frontera. A large pago of albariza west of Jerez, extending toward El Puerto (Balbaína Alta and Balbaína Baja), with exposure to the Atlantic poniente.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Añina. Which town?
cards.a: Jerez de la Frontera. A pago west of Jerez, on the road to Sanlúcar, with fine albariza and Atlantic exposure.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Los Tercios. Which town?
cards.a: Jerez de la Frontera. A pago between Jerez and El Puerto de Santa María, where the albariza is strongly Atlantic-influenced.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Miraflores. Which town?
cards.a: Sanlúcar de Barrameda. One of Sanlúcar's great pagos, just south of the town, with pure albariza close to the sea.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Maína. Which town?
cards.a: Sanlúcar de Barrameda. A pago east of Sanlúcar on the Loma de la Maína ridge, with albariza rich in diatom fossils.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Martín Miguel. Which town?
cards.a: Sanlúcar de Barrameda. A Sanlúcar pago on the Loma de Martín Miguel, north of the town, close to the Guadalquivir estuary and the Atlantic.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Pastrana. Which town?
cards.a: Sanlúcar de Barrameda. A pago on the edge of Sanlúcar whose albariza gives Hidalgo La Gitana's Pastrana Manzanilla Pasada, one of the first single-pago Sherries of the modern era.

cards.q: Find the albariza pago Callejuela. Which town?
cards.a: Sanlúcar de Barrameda. A pago just east of Sanlúcar, now associated with the Blanco brothers' Bodegas Callejuela, growers who began bottling their own single-pago manzanillas and vintage wines.

cards.q: Find Jerez-Xérès-Sherry. Which three towns formed the historic triangle?
cards.a: Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María and Sanlúcar de Barrameda; since 2021 Sherry may be aged anywhere in the production zone.

cards.q: What must a Manzanilla be?
cards.a: A biologically aged Palomino Sherry aged in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, where coastal humidity keeps the flor thick; a separate DO since 1964.

cards.q: What is albariza?
cards.a: A white, chalky marl rich in diatoms that holds winter rain and bakes to a crust in summer; the best Sherry pagos (Macharnudo, Carrascal, Balbaína, Añina, Miraflores).

cards.q: Fino and Manzanilla: ageing and alcohol?
cards.a: Fortified to 15 to 15.5% abv, aged biologically under flor in a solera, bone dry, pale; minimum 2 years (Manzanilla Pasada and Fino Antiguo 7 years since the 2021 reform).

cards.q: Amontillado, Oloroso and Palo Cortado: how do they differ?
cards.a: Amontillado begins under flor and then ages oxidatively; Oloroso is fortified to about 17 to 18% abv and ages oxidatively from the start; Palo Cortado has Amontillado finesse with Oloroso body.

cards.q: What changed in the Sherry rules in 2021?
cards.a: Unfortified Fino and Manzanilla allowed if they reach 15% naturally; ageing allowed across the whole zone; six old varieties re-admitted; 7-year minimum for Manzanilla Pasada and Fino Antiguo.

cards.q: What are VOS and VORS Sherries?
cards.a: Vinum Optimum Signatum (average age over 20 years) and Vinum Optimum Rare Signatum (over 30 years), certified by tasting and analysis; 12- and 15-year categories also exist.

cards.q: What are Pale Cream, Medium and Cream Sherry?
cards.a: Sweetened blends (vinos generosos de licor): Pale Cream is Fino sweetened with rectified must; Medium is usually Amontillado-based; Cream is Oloroso with PX.

cards.q: Find Montilla-Moriles. What is different from Jerez?
cards.a: Pedro Ximénez reaches 15% naturally, so finos are often unfortified; hotter, inland near Córdoba; albero soils; Amontillado means "in the style of Montilla".

cards.q: What did Francis Drake do in 1587 that made Sherry popular in England?
cards.a: He raided Cádiz and seized 2,900 butts of sack (Sherry).

decks.title: Port: categories and quintas
decks.description: The Douro sub-regions, the great quintas and every Port category.

cards.q: Find Quinta do Vallado. What is it known for?
cards.a: Douro Boys estate, Baixo Corgo.

cards.q: Find Quinta da Pacheca. What is it known for?
cards.a: Estate and wine hotel, Baixo Corgo.

cards.q: Find Quinta da Gaivosa. What is it known for?
cards.a: Alves de Sousa estate, Baixo Corgo.

cards.q: Find Quinta do Côtto. What is it known for?
cards.a: Historic Baixo Corgo estate.

cards.q: Find Quinta do Noval. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Passadouro. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Cruzeiro. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta da Cavadinha. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta da Roêda. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Bomfim. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta da Foz. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta das Carvalhas. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta de la Rosa. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Junco. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta de Terra Feita. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Portal. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Infantado. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta Nova de Nossa Senhora do Carmo. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Panascal. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta de São Luiz. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta de Nápoles. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta de Roriz. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta da Romaneira. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta dos Malvedos. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta do Tua. What is it known for?
cards.a: Graham's quinta, Tua valley.

cards.q: Find Quinta de Vargellas. What is it known for?
cards.a: Taylor's single-quinta Vintage, first released 1958.

cards.q: Find Quinta dos Canais. What is it known for?
cards.a: Cockburn's quinta.

cards.q: Find Quinta do Vesuvio. What is it known for?
cards.a: Symington estate, foot-trodden single-quinta Vintage.

cards.q: Find Quinta da Senhora da Ribeira. What is it known for?
cards.a: Dow's quinta, Douro Superior.

cards.q: Find Quinta do Vale Meão. What is it known for?

cards.q: Find Quinta de Ervamoira. What is it known for?
cards.a: Ramos Pinto estate and museum, Côa valley.

cards.q: Find Quinta da Leda. What is it known for?
cards.a: Casa Ferreirinha estate, Barca Velha source.

cards.q: Find the Baixo Corgo.
cards.a: The westernmost, wettest and coolest Douro sub-region (Régua); lighter ruby and basic tawny.

cards.q: Find the Cima Corgo.
cards.a: The heart of quality Port around Pinhão, with most of the great quintas.

cards.q: Find the Douro Superior.
cards.a: The hottest, driest and most remote sub-region, to the Spanish border; Vargellas, Vesuvio, Vale Meão.

cards.q: On what rock do Douro vineyards grow?
cards.a: Pre-Cambrian schist, broken up by hand to make terraces (socalcos, patamares, vinha ao alto); granite only at the edges.

cards.q: Vintage Port: rules?
cards.a: From a single declared year, approved by the IVDP; bottled in the second or third year after harvest; ages in bottle and throws a crust.

cards.q: LBV Port: rules?
cards.a: Late Bottled Vintage: single-year ruby bottled after 4 to 6 years in wood; filtered or unfiltered.

cards.q: Colheita and aged tawny Port: rules?
cards.a: Colheita is a single-vintage tawny with at least 7 years in cask. Tawnies with indication of age: 10, 20, 30, 40 and (since 2021) 50 years old, describing average style.

cards.q: Reserve and Crusted Port?
cards.a: Reserve ruby: a premium blend; Reserve tawny: at least 6 to 7 years in wood. Crusted: a blend of several years bottled unfiltered and aged at least 3 years in bottle.

cards.q: How is Port fortified?
cards.a: Fermentation (2 to 3 days in lagares or autovinifiers) is stopped by adding aguardente at about 77% abv, roughly one part to four, giving 19 to 22% abv and 80 to 120 g/l sugar.

cards.q: When was the Douro demarcated, and by whom?
cards.a: 10 September 1756, by the Marquis of Pombal, creating the Companhia Geral and one of the first demarcated wine regions.

cards.q: What was the Methuen Treaty?
cards.a: A 1703 Anglo-Portuguese treaty giving Portuguese wine lower duties in England than French wine, fuelling the Port trade.

decks.title: Madeira: grapes and styles
decks.description: The noble grapes, estufagem and canteiro, and age statements.

cards.q: Find Madeira. Name the four noble grapes and their sweetness.
cards.a: Sercial (dry), Verdelho (medium dry), Boal (medium rich), Malvasia (rich); Tinta Negra makes most Madeira at any sweetness.

cards.q: What is estufagem?
cards.a: Heating wine in stainless-steel tanks (estufas) to about 45 to 50 C for at least 3 months; used for younger, cheaper Madeira.

cards.q: What is canteiro?
cards.a: Ageing in cask for years in warm lodges without artificial heat; used for the best wines and required for Frasqueira.

cards.q: Madeira age categories?
cards.a: Seleccionado (3 years), Rainwater (pale, medium dry, up to about 5 years), 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 and over 40 years (Reserva, Reserva Especial, Reserva Extra).

cards.q: Colheita and Frasqueira Madeira?
cards.a: Colheita: single vintage, 85% from one year, at least 5 years in cask, bottling date on label. Frasqueira (Garrafeira): single vintage, at least 20 years in cask.

cards.q: When is Madeira fortified?
cards.a: With 96% grape spirit: early in fermentation for sweet Boal and Malvasia, late for dry Sercial and Verdelho; final 17 to 22% abv.

cards.q: Find Jardim da Serra.
cards.a: High, cool vineyards above Câmara de Lobos, good for Sercial.

cards.q: Find Câmara de Lobos.
cards.a: Fishing town at the heart of Madeira's south-coast vineyards; Tinta Negra on terraced poios.

cards.q: Find Seixal.
cards.a: North-coast terraces for Sercial.

cards.q: Find Fajã dos Padres.
cards.a: Historic coastal vineyard of Malvasia Cândida, reachable by cliff lift.

cards.q: What struck Madeira in 1852 to 1872?
cards.a: Oidium (powdery mildew) from 1852 and then phylloxera from 1872 devastated the vineyards.

cards.q: What has been allowed on Madeira labels for Tinta Negra since 2015?
cards.a: The variety name; previously only the four noble varieties could appear.

decks.title: Germany: the 13 Anbaugebiete
decks.description: Each German quality-wine region with its grapes and soils.

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Mosel. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Riesling (about 62%), Müller-Thurgau, Elbling, Weißburgunder, Spätburgunder, Kerner. Devonian slate in blue, grey and red forms, steep south-facing slopes over a river that reflects light and buffers frost (about 8536 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Rheingau. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Riesling (about 76%), Spätburgunder. A south-facing slope sheltered by the Taunus with the wide Rhine as a mirror; loess and marl near the river, slate and quartzite higher up (about 3207 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Pfalz. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Riesling, Dornfelder, Müller-Thurgau, Spätburgunder, Grauburgunder, Weißburgunder. Sheltered by the Haardt forest; sandstone, limestone, loess and basalt (about 23793 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Nahe. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Riesling, Müller-Thurgau, Dornfelder, Grauburgunder, Weißburgunder. Slate, quartzite, porphyry, melaphyre, sandstone and loess in a sunny, dry valley (about 4250 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Rheinhessen. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Dornfelder, Silvaner, Grauburgunder, Spätburgunder. A warm, dry plateau; loess and marl over limestone, red Rotliegend slate at the Roter Hang (about 27499 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Franken. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Silvaner, Müller-Thurgau, Bacchus, Riesling, Domina, Spätburgunder. Triassic layers of red sandstone, shell limestone and Keuper; continental climate with frost risk (about 6173 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Baden. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Spätburgunder, Müller-Thurgau, Grauburgunder, Weißburgunder, Riesling, Gutedel. Warm Upper Rhine plain between Black Forest and Vosges; granite, volcanic tuff, loess, limestone and moraine (about 15679 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Ahr. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Spätburgunder, Frühburgunder, Riesling. Devonian slate and greywacke on steep terraces that store heat in a sheltered valley (about 531 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Württemberg. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Trollinger, Riesling, Lemberger, Schwarzriesling, Spätburgunder. Steep Neckar slopes of Muschelkalk and Keuper marl; warm summers (about 11392 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Mittelrhein. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Riesling, Spätburgunder, Müller-Thurgau. Slate and greywacke terraces above the Rhine (about 460 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Hessische Bergstraße. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Riesling, Grauburgunder, Spätburgunder, Müller-Thurgau. Granite and loess on the western edge of the Odenwald (about 461 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Saale-Unstrut. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Müller-Thurgau, Weißburgunder, Silvaner, Riesling, Bacchus. Muschelkalk and sandstone terraces in a dry continental climate (about 853 ha).

cards.q: Find the Anbaugebiet Sachsen. Main grapes and terroir?
cards.a: Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Weißburgunder, Grauburgunder, Traminer, Goldriesling. Granite, syenite and gneiss on south-facing Elbe terraces (about 522 ha).

cards.q: How many Anbaugebiete does Germany have? Largest and smallest?
cards.a: 13. Rheinhessen is the largest (about 27,000 ha), then Pfalz; the Hessische Bergstrasse, Mittelrhein, Sachsen and Ahr are the smallest (about 450 to 550 ha each).

cards.q: Which two Anbaugebiete lie in the former East Germany?
cards.a: Saale-Unstrut and Sachsen, the northernmost and easternmost.

cards.q: Find the Saar. Which Bereich, and why famous?
cards.a: A Bereich of the Mosel on its tributary: cool, steep slate; Scharzhofberg (Egon Müller), Kanzem, Ayl, Ockfen.

cards.q: Find the Ruwer.
cards.a: Small Mosel tributary; Maximin Grünhaus and Karthäuserhof monopoles.

cards.q: Name the two Bereiche of the Pfalz.
cards.a: Mittelhaardt-Deutsche Weinstrasse (Forst, Deidesheim, Wachenheim) and Südliche Weinstrasse.

decks.title: Germany: famous Einzellagen
decks.description: The great single vineyards from the Saar to Franken.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Bernkasteler Doctor. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A steep, south-facing slate slope of only about 3.3 hectares directly above the rooftops of Bernkastel, and Germany's most famous vineyard.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Wehlener Sonnenuhr. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A sweep of blue slate facing south-west across the Mosel from Wehlen, named for the sundial Jodocus Prüm built among the vines in 1842 so pickers could tell the time.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Graacher Himmelreich. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. 'Kingdom of heaven' rises above Graach between Bernkastel and Wehlen on deep, stony blue slate.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Ürziger Würzgarten. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. The 'spice garden' is a near-vertical cliff of red Rotliegend slate and volcanic rock above Ürzig, where vines grow in pockets between rock outcrops.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Erdener Prälat. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A tiny strip of red slate between rock walls and the river opposite Erden, the warmest microclimate on the Mosel.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Erdener Treppchen. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. The 'little staircase' takes its name from the steps cut into the rock so growers could reach the vines.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Brauneberger Juffer-Sonnenuhr. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. The heart of the Juffer slope across the river from Brauneberg, with its own sundial.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Piesporter Goldtröpfchen. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A south-facing amphitheatre of blue slate curving behind the village of Piesport, the 'little gold drop' is one of the Mosel's most perfect sites, making juicy, peachy Riesling.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Trittenheimer Apotheke. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A steep slate slope in the river bend at Trittenheim, the first great site of the Middle Mosel heading downstream from Trier.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Scharzhofberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A single steep, south-facing slope of grey slate in a side valley of the Saar near Wiltingen, about 28 hectares, and arguably the greatest Riesling vineyard in the world.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Ockfener Bockstein. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A steep grey-slate hillside above Ockfen on the Saar.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Saarburger Rausch. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A south-facing slope above Saarburg whose grey slate is laced with green diabase, a volcanic rock.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Kanzemer Altenberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A long, very steep slope on the Saar's left bank near Kanzem, owned in part by von Othegraven (since 2010 owned by TV presenter Günther Jauch) and Van Volxem.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Ayler Kupp. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A rounded hill of slate at Ayl on the Saar.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Bremmer Calmont. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. A cliff of slate on the Mosel's outside bend at Bremm, generally billed as the steepest vineyard in Europe, with a via ferrata climbing path through the vines.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Maximin Grünhäuser Abtsberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. The steep blue-slate slope rising directly behind the Grünhaus manor at Mertesdorf, once reserved for the abbot of St.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Eitelsbacher Karthäuserhofberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mosel. The Karthäuserhof's monopole, a south-facing slate slope above the estate at Eitelsbach, worked by the Carthusians from 1335.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Rüdesheimer Berg Schlossberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheingau. The steepest part of Rüdesheim's Berg, terraced quartzite and slate around the ruined Ehrenfels castle where the Rhine turns north into the gorge.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Steinberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheingau. A walled vineyard of about 37 hectares below Kloster Eberbach, laid out by the Cistercians in the twelfth century and enclosed by a wall completed in the eighteenth.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Erbacher Marcobrunn. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheingau. A low-lying site on deep marl next to the Marcobrunn spring on the border of Erbach and Hattenheim, long the most expensive Rheingau vineyard.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Hochheimer Hölle. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheingau. A south-facing slope above the Main at Hochheim, the warm eastern outpost of the Rheingau.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Kiedricher Gräfenberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheingau. A steep slope of phyllite slate behind the Gothic village of Kiedrich, high on the Rheingau slope.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Rauenthaler Baiken. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheingau. A high site on phyllite and loess at Rauenthal, historically one of the Rheingau's most expensive, giving spicy, firm Riesling.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Niederhäuser Hermannshöhle. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Nahe. The Nahe's most celebrated vineyard, a steep slope above the river at Niederhausen of grey slate mixed with porphyry and melaphyre.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Schlossböckelheimer Kupfergrube. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Nahe. A vineyard cut from the spoil of an old copper mine by the Prussian state domain in the early 1900s, with convict labour.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Monzinger Halenberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Nahe. A steep slope of blue slate and quartzite at Monzingen on the upper Nahe.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Niersteiner Pettenthal. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheinhessen. The steepest part of the Roter Hang, a cliff of red Permian slate rising directly from the Rhine north of Nierstein.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Nackenheimer Rothenberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheinhessen. The northern end of the Roter Hang at Nackenheim, steep red slate overlooking the Rhine and protected as a nature reserve.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Westhofener Morstein. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Rheinhessen. A limestone and clay slope near Westhofen in the Wonnegau, now among Germany's most famous dry Riesling sites thanks to Keller and Wittmann.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Forster Kirchenstück. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Pfalz. A walled vineyard of under 4 hectares behind Forst's church, ranked at the top of the 1828 Bavarian tax survey.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Forster Jesuitengarten. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Pfalz. Neighbour of the Kirchenstück, once owned by the Jesuits, on sandy loam with basalt.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Forster Pechstein. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Pfalz. Named after the black basalt ('pitch stone') quarried from the Pechsteinkopf above Forst and scattered through its soil, the only basalt in the Pfalz's great sites.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Kallstadter Saumagen. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Pfalz. A former Roman limestone quarry turned vineyard at Kallstadt, named after its shape (a stuffed pig's stomach, the local dish).

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Birkweiler Kastanienbusch. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Pfalz. A high, steep slope on the edge of the Palatinate Forest at Birkweiler, with red Rotliegend slate, sandstone and granite.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Achkarrer Schlossberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Baden. A steep volcanic hill crowned by a ruined castle above Achkarren on the Kaiserstuhl.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Ihringer Winklerberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Baden. Terraced volcanic slopes at Ihringen, the hottest spot in Germany, protected as a nature reserve for its rare plants and lizards.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Würzburger Stein. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Franken. Germany's largest famous single vineyard, about 85 hectares of shell limestone rising above the Main north of Würzburg.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Escherndorfer Lump. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Franken. A steep curve of shell limestone on the Volkach Main loop.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Franken. A Keuper slope below the Schwanberg at Iphofen in the Steigerwald, named after Prince-Bishop Julius Echter.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Bürgstadter Centgrafenberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Franken. A red sandstone slope on the lower Main at Bürgstadt, source of Rudolf Fürst's famous Spätburgunder and Riesling.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Walporzheimer Kräuterberg. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Ahr. A tiny, terraced amphitheatre of slate at Walporzheim, so hot that wild herbs grow between the vines.

cards.q: Find the Einzellage Bopparder Hamm. Which Anbaugebiet?
cards.a: Mittelrhein. A sweeping slate slope in the biggest loop of the Rhine at Boppard, divided into sites such as Feuerlay, Mandelstein and Ohlenberg, giving lively, mineral Riesling.

cards.q: Order the Prädikate from least to most ripe.
cards.a: Kabinett, Spätlese, Auslese, Beerenauslese (BA), Eiswein, Trockenbeerenauslese (TBA); Eiswein has the BA must weight but from frozen grapes.

cards.q: What is the VDP classification pyramid?
cards.a: Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage, Grosse Lage; a dry Grosse Lage wine is a Grosses Gewächs (GG).

cards.q: What did the 2021 German wine law reform introduce?
cards.a: An origin-based pyramid (Deutscher Wein, Landwein, Gutswein, Ortswein, Lagenwein) like the Romance model; Grosslagen names restricted and Erste and Grosse Lage terms regulated.

cards.q: What did the 1971 German wine law do?
cards.a: Based quality on must weight (Prädikate), consolidated about 30,000 sites into about 2,600 Einzellagen and created the Grosslagen.

cards.q: Which rock dominates the Mosel?
cards.a: Devonian slate (blue, grey and red), which drains and stores heat on steep south-facing slopes.

decks.title: Austria: the DACs
decks.description: All 18 DACs with their grapes and first vintages.

cards.q: Find the DAC Weinviertel. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner (DAC); many others under Niederösterreich. First DAC: from 2002 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Süd-Oststeiermark. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Welschriesling, Weißburgunder, Morillon, Grauburgunder, Riesling, Gelber Muskateller, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer. DAC from 2018 vintage (PDO 1996 as Süd-Oststeiermark).

cards.q: Find the DAC Thermenregion. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Zierfandler, Rotgipfler, Weißburgunder, Chardonnay, Sankt Laurent, Pinot Noir. DAC from 2023 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Weststeiermark. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Blauer Wildbacher (Schilcher); white varieties at Ort and Ried level. DAC from 2018 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Eisenberg. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Blaufränkisch; Welschriesling only with a Ried name. DAC from 2009 vintage (EU reg. 2011).

cards.q: Find the DAC Traisental. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner, Riesling. DAC from 2006 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Neusiedlersee. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Zweigelt (dry DAC); white varieties for sweet DAC. DAC from 2011 vintage (sweet wines added 2020; PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Wagram. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner, Roter Veltliner, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Noir and others by tier. DAC from 2021 vintage (PDO 1996 as Donauland; renamed 2007).

cards.q: Find the DAC Mittelburgenland. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Blaufränkisch. DAC from 2005 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Carnuntum. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch; Grüner Veltliner, Chardonnay, Weißburgunder. DAC from 2019 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Leithaberg. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Blaufränkisch (red); Weißburgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Grüner Veltliner and blends (white). DAC red from 2008, white from 2009 (EU reg. 2009).

cards.q: Find the DAC Südsteiermark. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Sauvignon Blanc, Morillon, Gelber Muskateller, Weißburgunder, Grauburgunder, Welschriesling, Riesling, Traminer. DAC from 2018 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Wachau. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner, Riesling (Riedenwein only these two); 17 varieties for Gebietswein. DAC from 2020 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Kamptal. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner, Riesling. DAC from 2008 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Kremstal. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner, Riesling. DAC from 2007 vintage (PDO 1996).

cards.q: Find the DAC Ruster Ausbruch. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: One or more white varieties: Furmint, Welschriesling, Weißburgunder, Chardonnay, Gelber Muskateller and others. DAC from October 2020.

cards.q: Find the DAC Rosalia. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: Blaufränkisch, Zweigelt (red); rosé from one or more red varieties. DAC from 2017 vintage.

cards.q: Find the DAC Wiener Gemischter Satz. Grapes and first DAC vintage?
cards.a: At least three white varieties from one vineyard, planted together. DAC from 2013 vintage.

cards.q: How many DACs does Austria have, and which was the last?
cards.a: 18 (counting Ruster Ausbruch and Wiener Gemischter Satz); Thermenregion became a DAC in 2023 and Weinviertel was the first (2002 vintage).

cards.q: What three tiers do most DACs use?
cards.a: Gebietswein (regional), Ortswein (village) and Riedenwein (single vineyard, named "Ried").

cards.q: Which federal state names replace a DAC when a wine fails the typicity rules?
cards.a: Niederösterreich, Burgenland, Steiermark or Wien, e.g. a Kamptal Chardonnay is labelled Niederösterreich.

cards.q: What was the 1985 Austrian wine scandal?
cards.a: A few brokers added diethylene glycol to sweeten wines; it led to one of the strictest wine laws in Europe and a turn to dry, quality wine.

decks.title: Wachau: Rieden and Vinea categories
decks.description: Great Wachau vineyards on gneiss, plus Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd.

cards.q: Find Ried Achleiten in the Wachau.
cards.a: A steep slope of terraced gneiss, amphibolite and serpentine above Weißenkirchen, facing south-east over the Danube.

cards.q: Find Ried Klaus in the Wachau.
cards.a: A narrow, steep terrace of gneiss next to the Achleiten at Weißenkirchen and Joching, giving taut, saline Riesling.

cards.q: Find Ried Loibenberg in the Wachau.
cards.a: The broad, south-facing hillside above Unterloiben and Oberloiben, one of the warmest sites in the Wachau, of gneiss covered in places with loess.

cards.q: Find Ried Kellerberg in the Wachau.
cards.a: Terraces of gneiss between Dürnstein and Oberloiben, cooled by air flowing down a side gully at night.

cards.q: Find Ried Steinertal in the Wachau.
cards.a: A cool, narrow side valley east of the Loibenberg with gneiss and amphibolite, where the temperature drops sharply at night.

cards.q: Find Ried Schütt in the Wachau.
cards.a: A site at the mouth of a side valley at Unterloiben whose name refers to the scree washed down from the hills; gravelly gneiss gives powerful yet clear Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.

cards.q: Find Ried Höhereck in the Wachau.
cards.a: A high, steep site between Dürnstein and Loiben on gneiss and mica schist, giving finely structured Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.

cards.q: Find Ried Singerriedel in the Wachau.
cards.a: A steep, terraced amphitheatre of mica schist and gneiss behind Spitz, facing south-east.

cards.q: Find Ried Steinriegl.
cards.a: A terraced Weissenkirchen Ried on gneiss above the Danube.

cards.q: Find Ried Tausend-Eimer-Berg (1000-Eimerberg).
cards.a: Spitz Ried on gneiss and mica schist; its name boasts of a thousand buckets of wine.

cards.q: Find Ried Liebenberg.
cards.a: Dürnstein Ried, steep terraces on gneiss.

cards.q: Steinfeder, Federspiel, Smaragd: what are they?
cards.a: Vinea Wachau categories for dry, unoaked wines: Steinfeder up to 11.5% abv, Federspiel up to 12.5%, Smaragd at least 12.5%; named after a grass, falconry and an emerald lizard.

cards.q: Wachau DAC: what is allowed at Riedenwein level?
cards.a: Only Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, dry, hand-harvested; no chaptalisation or oak flavour in the Vinea categories. DAC since the 2020 vintage.

cards.q: What rock underlies the great Wachau Rieden?
cards.a: Gneiss and amphibolite (primary rock) with loess on lower slopes; dry-stone terraces.

decks.title: Tokaj: villages, dűlők and styles
decks.description: The 27 settlements, the first growths and every Tokaji style.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Tarcal. What is it known for?
cards.a: Tarcal sits on the south-western foot of Tokaj hill, where loess drapes the volcanic core. It holds some of the region's most storied sites (Mézes Mály, Szarvas, Lónyai, Váti, Kassai), the Tokaj viticulture research station where Zéta and Kabar were bred, the Andrássy manor and Királyudvar's winery in a former royal court.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Tokaj. What is it known for?
cards.a: The town that gave the region its name sits at the point of Tokaj hill (Kopasz-hegy, 514 m) where the Bodrog flows into the Tisza. River traffic once carried barrels north to Poland.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Mád. What is it known for?
cards.a: Mád has the densest concentration of historic first-class vineyards in Tokaj: Szent Tamás, Úrágya, Betsek, Király, Nyulászó, Birsalmás, Percze and Danczka all surround the village, on rhyolite, andesite and quartzite. Royal Tokaji, Szepsy, Barta and Holdvölgy are based here, and the restored baroque synagogue recalls the Jewish merchants who ran much of the Tokaji trade until 1944.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Tállya. What is it known for?
cards.a: Tállya, a large market village on the western side of the hills, sits among andesite and rhyolite slopes with dűlők such as Hasznos and Dorgó. Its vineyards were among the Rákóczi family's holdings, and Lajos Kossuth, born in nearby Monok in 1802, was baptised in its Lutheran church.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Bodrogkeresztúr. What is it known for?
cards.a: Bodrogkeresztúr lies on the Bodrog under the eastern face of Tokaj hill. The Lapis vineyard above it, a terraced rhyolite slope, is the source of Királyudvar's best wines, and the village has given its name to several fine Szamorodni.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Erdőbénye. What is it known for?
cards.a: A forested village in a side valley at the northern edge of the Tokaj hills, Erdőbénye was the region's cooperage centre, making the 136-litre Gönc casks and smaller barrels from local Zemplén oak. Máté Szepsi Laczkó served as pastor here; his memorial house stands on the main street.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Olaszliszka. What is it known for?
cards.a: Olaszliszka, on the Bodrog, carries in its name the 'olasz' (Latin, Italian) settlers invited after the Mongol invasion. Szepsi Laczkó Máté taught here before becoming a pastor.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Sárospatak. What is it known for?
cards.a: Sárospatak, on the Bodrog in the north-east, was the seat of the Rákóczi princes. Their castle, the Reformed College founded in 1531 (where Comenius taught), and the Rákóczi cellar beneath the town anchor its history.

cards.q: Find the Tokaj village Sátoraljaújhely. What is it known for?
cards.a: The northernmost Tokaj town sits on the Slovak border, facing Slovenské Nové Mesto, which belonged to it until 1920. On its castle hill lies the Oremus vineyard, source of the legendary 1631 aszú attributed to Szepsi Laczkó Máté and the name that the Vega Sicilia-owned estate took for its brand.
