cards.a: A small, warm valley about an hour north of Christchurch, registered as a GI in 2018 and sitting within North Canterbury. Key grapes: Riesling, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the GI Waitaki Valley North Otago. What is it known for?
cards.a: One of New Zealand's newest and most marginal regions, in the Waitaki River valley around Kurow and Duntroon, registered in 2018. Its first vines went in around 2001. Key grapes: Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the GI Bannockburn. What is it known for?
cards.a: The most recent New Zealand wine GI, registered in February 2022, covering a small, warm sub-region of Central Otago on the southern bank of the Kawarau River near Cromwell. Key grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling, Pinot Gris.

cards.q: What are the Gimblett Gravels?
cards.a: An 800 ha district of stony former riverbed of the Ngaruroro in Hawke's Bay, defined by soil; Bordeaux blends and Syrah.

cards.q: What launched Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc internationally?
cards.a: Cloudy Bay's first vintage in 1985.

decks.title: South Africa: districts and wards
decks.description: The Wine of Origin units of the Cape.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Cape Coast. Its level and character?
cards.a: Overarching region within Western Cape. An overarching region that combines the Coastal Region and Cape South Coast, allowing blends of, say, Stellenbosch and Elgin fruit to name a coastal origin. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Karoo-Hoogland. Its level and character?
cards.a: Region within Northern Cape. A high-plateau region in the Northern Cape whose only district is Sutherland-Karoo, around one of South Africa's coldest towns. Its vineyards, at around 1,500 m, are the highest in South Africa. Key grapes: Shiraz, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Cape South Coast. Its level and character?
cards.a: Region within Cape Coast. The cool southern coastal region from Elgin to Plettenberg Bay, home to Walker Bay and its Hemel-en-Aarde wards, Elim and Elgin. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Klein Karoo. Its level and character?
cards.a: Region within Western Cape. The semi-arid valley along Route 62 from Montagu to the Langkloof, known for Calitzdorp's fortified wines, Muscadel and potstill brandy. Vines grow in kloofs and river valleys between ostrich farms. Key grapes: Muscat, Touriga Nacional, Chenin Blanc, Colombard.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Coastal Region. Its level and character?
cards.a: Region within Cape Coast. The Coastal Region includes South Africa's best-known districts: Cape Town, Stellenbosch, Paarl, Franschhoek, Wellington, Swartland, Tulbagh, Darling and Lutzville Valley. 'WO Coastal Region' usually indicates a blend across several of them. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Pinotage, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Swartland. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. The Swartland, the 'black land', takes its name from the renosterbos (rhino bush) that once darkened its rolling wheatfields north of Cape Town. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Grenache, Cinsault, Pinotage, Mourvèdre, Palomino.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Olifants River. Its level and character?
cards.a: Region within Western Cape. The region along the Olifants River from Citrusdal to Lutzville, with old mountain vineyards at Piekenierskloof and large irrigated cellars at Vredendal. It is citrus and rooibos country. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Grenache, Pinotage.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Breede River Valley. Its level and character?
cards.a: Region within Western Cape. The inland region of the Breedekloof, Worcester and Robertson districts, warm and irrigated, the source of a large share of South Africa's wine and brandy. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Chardonnay, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Cape West Coast. Its level and character?
cards.a: Subregion within Coastal Region. A subregion grouping the Atlantic-facing Darling and Lutzville Valley districts, St Helena Bay and the Bamboes Bay and Lamberts Bay wards, all cooled by the Benguela current. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Pinotage.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Sutherland-Karoo. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Karoo-Hoogland. A high-altitude, semi-arid district around Sutherland, South Africa's coldest town and home of the national astronomical observatory, with vineyards at about 1,500 m, the highest in the country. Key grapes: Shiraz, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Prince Albert. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Western Cape. A district around the Karoo town of Prince Albert below the Swartberg, with the wards Kweekvallei, Prince Albert Valley and Swartberg. Its few vineyards make small volumes for local producers. Key grapes: Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Central Drakensberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within KwaZulu-Natal. A district in the foothills of the Drakensberg near Winterton. Its vineyards at about 1,000 m face summer rainfall and hail. Key grapes: Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Overberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. A broad district of wheatfields and mountains east of Elgin, with wards at Elandskloof/Kaaimansgat, Greyton, Klein River, Shaw's Mountain and Theewater. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Worcester. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Breede River Valley. The Worcester district is the brandy capital of South Africa, with the largest distillery of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere, and a major source of bulk and branded wine. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Shiraz, Muscadel.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Nuveld-Karoo. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Western Cape. A district on the high Karoo plateau inland of the Cape fold mountains, listed on the February 2026 schedule with no wards. Its vineyards are among the most remote in South Africa.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Ceres Plateau. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Western Cape. A high plateau north-east of Ceres at about 1,000 m, apple and pear country whose cool vineyards supply sought-after Chenin and Pinot to Cape producers. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Central Orange River. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Northern Cape. The most northerly winegrowing area of the Cape, along about 350 km of the Orange River around Upington, Keimoes and Kakamas. Changed from a ward to a district after a 2019 proposal, it has five wards. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Muscat d'Alexandrie, Pinotage, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Swellendam. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. A district around the historic town of Swellendam (1743), the third-oldest in South Africa, with wards Buffeljags, Malgas and Stormsvlei. Key grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Robertson. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Breede River Valley. The 'valley of vines and roses' along the Breede River is the only part of the Cape with significant lime-rich soils, which also suit its many racehorse studs. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Colombard, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Muscadel.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Douglas. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Northern Cape. A district around Douglas, near the confluence of the Orange and Vaal rivers, with irrigated vineyards. Like the Central Orange River vineyards, it depends on irrigation in a hot, arid climate. Key grapes: Colombard, Chenin Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Lions River. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within KwaZulu-Natal. A district in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands near Howick, at about 1,000 to 1,200 m. Summer rainfall makes viticulture challenging, but cool nights suit Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Cape Town. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. A district named after the city, combining the wards of Constantia, Durbanville, Hout Bay and Philadelphia and the vineyards of the Cape Peninsula, including Cape Point. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Muscat de Frontignan.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Cape Agulhas. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. The district at Africa's southern tip; almost all its vines are in the Elim ward. Strong winds and a cool ripening season produce pungent Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Calitzdorp. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Klein Karoo. A small Klein Karoo town that calls itself South Africa's port capital. Key grapes: Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barocca, Souzão, Muscat, Chenin Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Breedekloof. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Breede River Valley. A district around Rawsonville in the upper Breede River and its tributaries, below the Du Toitskloof mountains. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Pinotage, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Paarl. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. Paarl, named after the pearl-like granite domes of Paarl Mountain, lies north of Stellenbosch along the Berg River. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Walker Bay. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. The district around the whale-watching town of Hermanus, best known for the Hemel-en-Aarde ('heaven and earth') valley, where Tim Hamilton Russell planted Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in 1975 and made the Cape's first serious Burgundy-style wines. Key grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Stellenbosch. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. Stellenbosch is South Africa's most famous wine district and its intellectual centre. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Merlot, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Tulbagh. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. A horseshoe-shaped valley enclosed by the Groot Winterhoek, Witzenberg and Obiekwaberg mountains, about 90 minutes north of Cape Town. Key grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Mourvèdre, Pinotage.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Citrusdal Mountain. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Olifants River. The mountain district above the Citrusdal valley, whose old, dry-farmed bush vines on sandstone are among the most prized in the new South Africa. Key grapes: Grenache, Chenin Blanc, Palomino, Pinotage.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Darling. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape West Coast. Darling, an hour north of Cape Town on the west coast, is famous for spring wild flowers and for cool Sauvignon Blanc. Its Groenekloof ward is one of the closest in South Africa to the cold Atlantic. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Citrusdal Valley. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Olifants River. The citrus-growing southern Olifants River valley around Citrusdal and Clanwilliam, irrigated from the Clanwilliam Dam. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Pinotage.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Wellington. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. A district north of Paarl at the foot of the Hawequa mountains, about 45 minutes from Cape Town. Key grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Elgin. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. Elgin is a high basin about an hour east of Cape Town, ringed by the Hottentots Holland mountains, which grew most of South Africa's apples before its farmers began planting vines in the late 1980s. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Still Bay. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. A coastal district around Stilbaai on the Garden Route, with the Goukou River Valley ward. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Plettenberg Bay. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. The newest and furthest-east district on the Cape South Coast, in mountainous terrain about 20 km east of Plettenberg Bay. The first vines were planted in 2000 (Bramon, known for Cap Classique). Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Lutzville Valley. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape West Coast. A district near the mouth of the Olifants River with large irrigated vineyards, including the Lutzville co-operative. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Colombard.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Lamberts Bay. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Cape West Coast. A coastal ward around the fishing town of Lamberts Bay, cooled by the Benguela current. Its vineyards, among the coolest on the west coast, mostly grow Sauvignon Blanc. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Elim. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Cape Agulhas. Elim's vineyards lie near Cape Agulhas, Africa's southernmost point, around the Moravian mission village of Elim, founded in 1824 and a national monument. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Shiraz, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Langeberg-Garcia. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Klein Karoo. A district along the Langeberg range around the Garcia Pass near Riversdale. Key grapes: Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Bot River. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Walker Bay. The gateway to Walker Bay, from the Bot River lagoon into the foothills of the Groenlandberg and Babylonstoren ranges, bordering the Kogelberg Biosphere. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Piekenierskloof. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Citrusdal Mountain. A high plateau above the Piekenierskloof Pass south of Citrusdal, with some of South Africa's oldest Grenache and Palomino vineyards. Key grapes: Grenache, Chenin Blanc, Palomino, Pinotage, Cinsault.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Franschhoek. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Coastal Region. Franschhoek, the 'French corner', is the valley where the VOC settled Huguenot refugees after 1688. Key grapes: Sémillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Porseleinberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Swartland. A ward named after the 'porcelain mountain' between Riebeek-Kasteel and the Berg River, whose blue-grey schist soils Boekenhoutskloof chose for its Porseleinberg Syrah, farmed organically by Callie Louw since the first vintage in 2010. Key grapes: Syrah.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Swartberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Prince Albert. A ward in the Swartberg mountains above Prince Albert. Its few hectares of vines grow in a dry, high-altitude setting where cold nights preserve acidity. Key grapes: Shiraz.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Lower Duivenhoks River. Its level and character?
cards.a: District within Cape South Coast. A small district along the lower Duivenhoks River between Heidelberg and the coast at Witsand. Its few vineyards benefit from sea breezes off the Indian Ocean near Witsand. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Durbanville. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Cape Town. Rolling wheat-and-vine country on the northern edge of Cape Town, whose hills catch Atlantic breezes and night-time mist. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinotage.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Paardeberg/Perdeberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Swartland. The granite massif of the Paardeberg (Perdeberg in Afrikaans), on the border of the Swartland and Paarl, is the spiritual home of the Swartland revival. Eben Sadie's farm and cellar, A.A. Key grapes: Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Grenache, Cinsault, Mourvèdre.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Riebeekberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Swartland. The slopes of the Kasteelberg around the villages of Riebeek-Kasteel and Riebeek-West, where the Mullineuxs farm their Roundstone vineyard on schist and iron-rich soils. Key grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Grenache, Mourvèdre.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Voor-Paardeberg. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Paarl. The southern and eastern side ('voor', in front of) the Paardeberg, the granite massif between Paarl and the Swartland. Key grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, Cinsault.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Simonsberg-Stellenbosch. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Stellenbosch. The southern and western slopes of the granite Simonsberg (1,390 m) north-east of Stellenbosch, one of the most prestigious wards in South Africa and among the first to be demarcated. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage, Merlot, Shiraz, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Simonsberg-Paarl. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Paarl. The north-eastern slopes of the Simonsberg facing Paarl, on decomposed granite. Glen Carlou, Plaisir de Merle, Backsberg and Rupert & Rothschild make Bordeaux blends and Chardonnay here. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Chardonnay, Merlot.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Bamboes Bay. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Cape West Coast. One of South Africa's smallest wards, on the Atlantic coast north of Lamberts Bay, where Fryer's Cove's vineyards lie a few hundred metres from the ocean. Its Sauvignon Blanc is lean and saline. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Bottelary. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Stellenbosch. The Bottelary Hills north-west of Stellenbosch, a ridge of granite with views to Table Mountain, is old-vine Chenin and Pinotage country. Key grapes: Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Constantia. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Cape Town. Constantia is the cradle of Cape wine and the source of one of history's most famous sweet wines. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Muscat de Frontignan.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Walker Bay. The middle section of the Hemel-en-Aarde, further inland and slightly warmer, on lighter granite-derived and shale soils. Key grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Stanford Foothills. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Walker Bay. A ward on the foothills of the Kleinrivier mountains above the village of Stanford, east of the Hemel-en-Aarde. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Polkadraai Hills. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Stellenbosch. Hills west of Stellenbosch near the R310 and Polkadraai Road, open to cool breezes from both False Bay and the Atlantic. Key grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Hemel-en-Aarde Valley. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Walker Bay. The lowest of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards, closest to the sea at Hermanus. Key grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinotage, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Banghoek. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Stellenbosch. A high mountain bowl at the top of the Helshoogte Pass between Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, surrounded by the Simonsberg, Jonkershoek and Groot Drakenstein ranges. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Jonkershoek Valley. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Stellenbosch. A narrow, steep-sided valley running south-east from Stellenbosch town into the Jonkershoek mountains, one of the wettest and most enclosed parts of the district. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge. Its level and character?
cards.a: Ward within Walker Bay. The highest and furthest inland of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards, at the top of the valley around 300 m and above, with cooler nights. Key grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the Wine of Origin Greater Cape. Its level and character?
cards.a: Overarching geographical unit within Klein Karoo. An overarching unit created after a 2019 proposal that groups the Western Cape, Northern Cape and Eastern Cape geographical units, so that wines blended across provincial lines (for example Western Cape and Orange River fruit) can carry a Cape origin. Key grapes: All Cape varieties.

cards.q: What are the levels of the Wine of Origin scheme?
cards.a: Geographical unit (e.g. Western Cape), region (e.g. Coastal Region), district (e.g. Stellenbosch) and ward (e.g. Banghoek); a single-vineyard category also exists.

cards.q: What is a Cape Blend?
cards.a: A red blend with Pinotage, usually 30 to 70%, a term used by the Cape Winemakers Guild and many producers; not a legal category.

cards.q: When was the first wine made at the Cape?
cards.a: 2 February 1659, recorded by Jan van Riebeeck.

decks.title: Chile: key DOs
decks.description: Regions, subregions and zones from Elqui to Malleco.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle Central. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Central Valley region is the engine of Chilean wine: the long tectonic trough between the Andes and the coastal range from Santiago's Chacabuco province south to Cauquenes and Linares in Maule. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Merlot, Syrah, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, País, Carignan.

cards.q: Find the DO Atacama. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The northernmost of Chile's six viticultural regions, matching the administrative Región de Atacama and split into the Copiapó and Huasco valleys. Key grapes: Moscatel varieties and Pedro Jiménez (mostly for pisco); Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO Coquimbo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Chile's second viticultural region from the north, matching the Coquimbo administrative region and its three transverse valleys, Elqui, Limarí and Choapa. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah, Pinot Noir; Pedro Jiménez and Moscatel for pisco.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de Copiapó. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Subregion matching Copiapó province, a desert river oasis at about 27°S where table grapes and pisco grapes vastly outnumber wine vines. Key grapes: Moscatel varieties, Pedro Jiménez.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Maule. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Maule is Chile's biggest wine subregion by far. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Carmenère, Chardonnay, País, Carignan, Cinsault, Malbec.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Huasco. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Subregion matching Huasco province, where the Huasco river cuts from the Andes to the sea past Vallenar and Freirina. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah; Moscatel for pisco and pajarete.

cards.q: Find the DO Sur. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Southern region (Región del Sur) runs from the Ñuble river country to Malleco in Araucanía and contains the Itata, Bío-Bío and Malleco valleys. Key grapes: País, Cinsault, Moscatel de Alejandría, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Elqui. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Elqui Valley, about 500 km north of Santiago, is one of the clearest skies on Earth (hence its observatories) and the spiritual home of Chilean pisco. Key grapes: Syrah, Carmenère, Sauvignon Blanc, Pedro Jiménez; Moscatel and Pedro Jiménez for pisco.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Rapel. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Rapel subregion covers the O'Higgins administrative region, named after the Rapel river that forms where the Cachapoal and Tinguiririca join. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Merlot, Syrah, Malbec, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Maipo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Maipo is the historic heart of Chilean fine wine and the home of its most famous Cabernet Sauvignon. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Franc; some Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Limarí. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Limarí, about 400 km north of Santiago, holds something almost unique in Chile: limestone. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Choapa. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Choapa Valley, about 400 km north of Santiago, is where Chile is narrowest and the Andes and coastal range almost touch. Key grapes: Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the DO Aconcagua. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The viticultural region that matches the Valparaíso administrative region. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Loncomilla. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Loncomilla is the central zone of Maule, along the Loncomilla river: San Javier, Villa Alegre, Retiro, Parral, Linares, Yerbas Buenas, Colbún and Longaví communes.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de Colchagua. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Colchagua is Chile's red-wine showcase, the southern zone of Rapel running from the Andes past San Fernando and Santa Cruz to the Pacific at Pichilemu along the Tinguiririca river. Key grapes: Carmenère, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Malbec, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Carignan; Sauvignon Blanc near the coast.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Claro. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Claro is the northern zone of Maule, named after the river through Talca: Talca, San Clemente, Pencahue, Maule, Pelarco, San Rafael, Empedrado and Curepto communes. It runs from Andean San Clemente to the coastal slate of Empedrado.

cards.q: Find the DO Austral. What is it known for?
cards.a: Chile's southernmost viticultural region, defined in 1994 as running from Cautín province 'as far south as soil and climate allow the vine to grow'. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Gewürztraminer.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Malleco. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Malleco, about 550 km south of Santiago in Araucanía, is the subregion that proved southern Chile could make world-class white wine. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de Curicó. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Curicó, about 200 km south of Santiago, is where Chile's modern wine era began. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Carmenère, Chardonnay, País.

cards.q: Find the DO Vicuña. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Vicuña commune, the heart of the middle Elqui valley and home of Viña Falernia, where wide valley-floor vineyards sit at around 500 to 700 m between bare granite mountains.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Cachapoal. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Cachapoal is the northern zone of Rapel, following the Cachapoal river from the Andes past Rancagua to Lake Rapel. Its east, under the mountains (Requínoa, Machalí, Rengo), is Cabernet country, home to Altaïr and the Andes-side vineyards of Viña San Pedro. Key grapes: Carmenère, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de Osorno. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Osorno covers Osorno, San Pablo and Purranque communes in Los Lagos plus La Unión and Futrono in Los Ríos, near 40°S. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Aconcagua. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Aconcagua Valley is where Chile's fine-wine revival found its first great red. Key grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Syrah, Merlot; Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir near the coast.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Itata. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Itata is where Chilean wine began in earnest and where its oldest living vineyards remain. Key grapes: País, Cinsault, Moscatel de Alejandría, Carignan, Semillon, Corinto (Chasselas).

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Bío-Bío. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The Bío-Bío subregion follows Chile's second-longest river in the old frontier country of southern Chile: Yumbel, Nacimiento, Mulchén, Negrete and Laja communes. Key grapes: País, Moscatel de Alejandría, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Lontué. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Lontué is the southern zone of Curicó, along the Lontué river: Curicó, Molina and Sagrada Familia communes plus Río Claro in Talca province. It is the valley's productive centre, with large estates around Molina and Lontué.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Teno. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Teno is the northern zone of Curicó, along the Teno river and the Mataquito towards the coast: Teno, Romeral, Rauco, Hualañé and Vichuquén communes. It runs from Andean piedmont at Romeral through warm valley floor to coastal hills near Lake Vichuquén.

cards.q: Find the DO Ovalle. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Ovalle commune, the lower Limarí valley that includes the limestone hills of Talinay and Quebrada Seca near the coast. This is where Limarí's reputation for mineral Chardonnay and Pinot Noir is made, by Tabalí, Concha y Toro and others.

cards.q: Find the DO Molina. What is it known for?
cards.a: Area defined by Molina, Río Claro and Curicó communes. It holds San Pedro's vast estate at Lontué and Miguel Torres's winery near Curicó, where Torres began modernising Chilean winemaking in 1979.

cards.q: Find the DO Mulchén. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area defined by Mulchén, Nacimiento and Negrete communes, cool and rainy, planted to Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and aromatic whites. Labels may add the complement Entre Cordilleras.

cards.q: Find the DO Cauquenes. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Cauquenes is the epicentre of Chile's rediscovered heritage. On the granite hills of the coastal range, bush-trained, dry-farmed País and Carignan up to 100 to 200 years old grow without irrigation, ploughed by horse, picked into wooden boxes. Key grapes: País, Carignan, Cinsault, Malbec.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Tutuvén. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Tutuvén is Maule's southern-coastal zone, consisting only of Cauquenes commune, named after the Tutuvén river. It is the heart of Chile's dry-farmed old-vine country.

cards.q: Find the DO Portezuelo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area defined by Portezuelo, Ninhue, Quirihue and San Nicolás communes, the north-western coastal hills of Itata with some of its oldest dry-farmed País and Cinsault. Labels may add the complement Costa.

cards.q: Find the DO Peumo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area defined by Peumo, Pichidegua, Las Cabras and San Vicente communes in west Cachapoal: Chile's Carmenère grand cru in all but name.

cards.q: Find the DO Paiguano. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Paiguano commune (also spelled Paihuano), the upper Elqui where the Claro river valley climbs past Pisco Elqui towards Alcohuaz.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de San Antonio. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. The San Antonio Valley, matching San Antonio province on the coast west of Santiago, is the sharpest of Chile's cool-climate frontiers. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO San Javier. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching San Javier commune, the hub of Maule's old-vine revival. Gillmore at Villavicencio and the Bouchon family at Mingre farm dry-farmed Carignan, País and Cabernet in the coastal hills, and many VIGNO Carignans come from here.

cards.q: Find the DO Curepto. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Curepto commune near the Mataquito mouth, in the coastal secano, with old dry-farmed País and newer coastal plantings. Labels may add the complement Costa.

cards.q: Find the DO Buin. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area defined by Buin, Paine and San Bernardo communes, the Central Maipo heartland south of Santiago.

cards.q: Find the DO Pencahue. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Pencahue commune west of Talca, warm and relatively dry, known for ripe reds and dry-farmed old vines. Labels may add the complement Entre Cordilleras.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de Casablanca. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Casablanca turned Chile into a white-wine country. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah, Gewürztraminer.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle de Leyda. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Leyda is a zone of the San Antonio Valley, made of the San Juan (San Antonio commune) and Santo Domingo areas, and the name most cool-climate fans know. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Cautín. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Cautín, matching Perquenco and Galvarino communes in Araucanía, is a small, very cool subregion where a few producers grow Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc on volcanic soils under heavy rainfall. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find the DO Traiguén. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Traiguén commune in Malleco, where Viña Aquitania planted the Sol de Sol Chardonnay vineyard in the 1990s and Baettig and others have followed with taut Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Labels may add the complement Entre Cordilleras.

cards.q: Find the DO Santa Cruz. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area defined by Santa Cruz and Chépica communes, the tourist heart of Colchagua. It includes the Apalta horseshoe (now its own DO) and the town's Colchagua Museum; valley-floor vineyards here give generous Carmenère and Cabernet.

cards.q: Find the DO Requínoa. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Requínoa commune at the foot of the Andes in east Cachapoal. Altaïr, the San Pedro project created with Château Dassault in the early 2000s, and other Andes-side estates grow structured Cabernet blends on stony colluvial slopes.

cards.q: Find the DO Marchigüe. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Marchigüe commune, the west Colchagua frontier planted from the late 1990s, notably by Montes and Montgras. Rolling granite hills, a breeze from the Pacific and low rainfall give Syrah, Cabernet and Carmenère with freshness and grip.

cards.q: Find the DO Coelemu. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area defined by Coelemu and Treguaco communes near the mouth of the Itata. It includes Guarilihue, the granite hamlet where De Martino and others source century-old Cinsault and Moscatel for wines fermented in clay tinajas.

cards.q: Find the DO Lolol. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Lolol commune in west Colchagua, a valley of old adobe houses and newer hillside vineyards where coastal influence cools Syrah, Cabernet and Rhône varieties. Labels may add the complement Costa.

cards.q: Find the DO Paredones. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Paredones commune, Colchagua's coastal end about 10 to 15 km from the Pacific.

cards.q: Find the DO Valle del Marga-Marga. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. A small coastal subregion matching Quilpué commune, inland from Viña del Mar, listed directly under the Aconcagua region. It is cool, hilly and close to the sea, with only a few vineyards, mostly for white wine and Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find the DO Santo Domingo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area of the Valle de Leyda zone defined by Santo Domingo commune, south of the port of San Antonio near the Maipo river mouth. Coastal vineyards here are among the coolest in the zone.

cards.q: Find the DO Pirque. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Pirque commune, on the south bank of the Maipo where the river leaves the Andes.

cards.q: Find the DO San Juan. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area of the Valle de Leyda zone defined by San Antonio commune, covering much of the Leyda hills around the village of Leyda itself. Viña Leyda and Amayna farm here on granite with clay, a few kilometres from the sea.

cards.q: Find the DO Isla de Maipo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Isla de Maipo commune, an island-like tract between arms of the Maipo river in central Maipo. De Martino and Tarapacá are based here; the warm, alluvial valley floor produces ripe Cabernet, Carmenère and Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO Panquehue. What is it known for?
cards.a: Area matching Panquehue commune, the warm heart of the inland Aconcagua valley and home of Viña Errázuriz since 1870, with its Max Viñedo hillside vineyard and the Don Maximiano estate.

cards.q: Find the DO Puente Alto. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 1994. Area matching Puente Alto and La Pintana communes on the north bank of the Maipo: the most valuable Cabernet terroir in Chile. On a stony alluvial terrace at about 650 m sit Concha y Toro's Don Melchor vineyard, Almaviva and Viñedo Chadwick, side by side.

cards.q: Find the DO Lo Abarca. What is it known for?
cards.a: Lo Abarca is Chile's tiniest DO, about 44.5 ha around a hamlet 4 km from the Pacific in the San Antonio Valley, and in practice it is one producer's vineyard: Casa Marín, planted from 2000 by María Luz Marín against every adviser's warning. Key grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Noir, Syrah.

cards.q: Find the DO Apalta. What is it known for?
cards.a: Apalta is the most famous hillside in Chile: a horseshoe of granite slopes opening south onto the Tinguiririca river near Santa Cruz in Colchagua, recognised as its own DO in 2018 with about 1,007 ha of vineyards. Key grapes: Carmenère, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot, Malbec, Grenache, Mourvèdre, Carignan.

cards.q: Find the DO Chiloé. What is it known for?
cards.a: Chiloé became a Chilean DO subregion in 2025: Decree 27 of November 2024, published on 14 May 2025, added the whole archipelago of Chiloé province to the Austral region. Key grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling.

cards.q: Find the DO Secano Interior. What is it known for?
cards.a: Secano Interior ('dry interior') is a special denomination of origin for wines made only from País and Cinsault grown on unirrigated land in the coastal hills and interior of Maule, Ñuble and Biobío. Key grapes: País (Mission, Criolla), Cinsault.

cards.q: What are Costa, Entre Cordilleras and Andes?
cards.a: East-west zoning terms added to Chilean DOs in 2012 to show the cool coast, the warm central valley and the Andean foothills.

cards.q: When was Carmenère identified in Chile, and how?
cards.a: 1994: French ampelographer Jean-Michel Boursiquot recognised that much "Merlot" in Chile was Carmenère.

decks.title: Argentina: key IGs and DOCs
decks.description: Mendoza departments and districts, Salta, Patagonia.

cards.q: Find Patagonia. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. The Patagonia IG is an interprovincial umbrella for Neuquén, Río Negro, La Pampa, Chubut and the rest of southern Argentina. Key grapes: Malbec, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Semillon, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find Cuyo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. Cuyo is the interprovincial IG covering Mendoza, San Juan and San Luis, the historic western heartland that makes the vast majority of Argentine wine. Key grapes: Malbec, Bonarda, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cereza, Criolla Grande, Torrontés, Pedro Giménez.

cards.q: Find Río Negro. What is it known for?
cards.a: Río Negro's provincial IG covers about 1,300 ha (INV 2024), most along the irrigated Alto Valle of the Río Negro, an apple-and-pear valley where Humberto Canale planted vines in 1909.

cards.q: Find Córdoba Argentina. What is it known for?
cards.a: Córdoba's provincial IG (with 'Argentina' added to separate it from Spain's Córdoba) covers about 240 ha of vines (INV 2024).

cards.q: Find Salta. What is it known for?
cards.a: Salta is Argentina's altitude province: about 3,700 ha of vines (INV 2024), almost all in the Calchaquí valleys between 1,700 and 3,100 m. Key grapes: Malbec, Torrontés Riojano, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tannat, Cabernet Franc, Criolla Chica.

cards.q: Find Mendoza. What is it known for?
cards.a: Mendoza is the province that is Argentine wine to most of the world: about 142,800 ha of vines in 2024 (INV), more than 70% of the national vineyard and of the 2026 grape harvest. Key grapes: Malbec (39,856 ha in 2024), Bonarda, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cereza, Criolla Grande, Syrah, Chardonnay, Torrontés, Pedro Giménez.

cards.q: Find Catamarca. What is it known for?
cards.a: Catamarca's provincial IG covers about 2,700 ha of vines (INV 2024) in high Andean valleys: Fiambalá and Tinogasta in the west, Belén and Santa María in the north (where the Calchaquí valleys begin), and Pomán. Key grapes: Torrontés Riojano, Malbec, Syrah, Criolla, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find Neuquén. What is it known for?
cards.a: Neuquén's provincial IG covers about 1,500 ha (INV 2024), most of it created from scratch since the late 1990s on the desert plateau of San Patricio del Chañar, north of the city of Neuquén, where large irrigation projects turned steppe into vineyard for Bodega del Fin del Mundo, Familia Schroeder and NQN.

cards.q: Find La Rioja Argentina. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. La Rioja's provincial IG carries 'Argentina' in its name to avoid any confusion with Spain's Rioja. Key grapes: Torrontés Riojano, Malbec, Bonarda, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find San Juan. What is it known for?
cards.a: San Juan is Argentina's second wine province, about 39,700 ha of vines in 2024 (INV) and roughly a quarter of the national harvest. Key grapes: Syrah, Malbec, Bonarda, Cereza, Criolla Grande, Pedro Giménez, Moscatel de Alejandría, Torrontés.

cards.q: Find Jujuy. What is it known for?
cards.a: Jujuy, Argentina's northernmost wine province, has only about 70 ha of vines (INV 2024) but some of the most spectacular: terraces in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a UNESCO World Heritage valley, at 2,300 to over 3,000 m. Key grapes: Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Syrah, Merlot, Criolla.

cards.q: Find San Rafael. What is it known for?
cards.a: San Rafael is Mendoza's southern oasis, an irrigated plain at 450 to 800 m on the Diamante and Atuel rivers, about 230 km south of the city, with about 11,500 ha of vines (INV 2024).

cards.q: Find Valles Calchaquíes. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. The Calchaquí valleys form one of the highest wine regions on Earth: a 270-km chain of arid valleys along the Calchaquí river and its tributaries, crossing Salta, Tucumán and Catamarca from Cachi and Payogasta in the north to Cafayate and Santa María in the south. Key grapes: Malbec, Torrontés Riojano, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tannat, Cabernet Franc, Criolla Chica.

cards.q: Find Calingasta. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. Calingasta is San Juan's spectacular Andean valley, a north-south trough at 1,350 to 1,700 m between the main cordillera and the pre-cordillera, reached by a mountain road from San Juan.

cards.q: Find Tucumán. What is it known for?
cards.a: Tucumán's provincial IG covers a small wine area of about 145 ha (INV 2024), almost all in the Tafí del Valle department on the Calchaquí side of the mountains, at Colalao del Valle and Amaicha del Valle, where Malbec and Torrontés grow at about 1,700 to 2,000 m.

cards.q: Find Valle de Uco. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. The Uco Valley is where Argentine wine went uphill and found its future. Key grapes: Malbec (16,584 ha across its three departments in 2024), Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Semillon.

cards.q: Find General Alvear. What is it known for?
cards.a: General Alvear, east of San Rafael on the Atuel river, is Mendoza's southernmost wine department, with about 3,100 ha (INV 2024) of mostly traditional varieties and everyday wine.

cards.q: Find Añelo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Añelo department in Neuquén contains San Patricio del Chañar, where from the late 1990s irrigation turned desert plateau into vineyards for Bodega del Fin del Mundo, Familia Schroeder and NQN; it holds 89% of Neuquén's Malbec (INV 2024).

cards.q: Find San Carlos. What is it known for?
cards.a: San Carlos is the southern Uco department, about 8,800 ha of vines (INV 2024), two-thirds of them Malbec.

cards.q: Find Lavalle. What is it known for?
cards.a: Lavalle, north of Mendoza city, is the province's driest and lowest wine department (around 600 m), with about 12,300 ha of vines (INV 2024) for bulk wine, juice and grape concentrate.

cards.q: Find Quebrada de Humahuaca. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2015. The Quebrada de Humahuaca, a UNESCO World Heritage valley of coloured mountains in Jujuy, has a tiny modern wine scene on terraces between about 2,300 and 3,300 m around Maimará, Tilcara, Huacalera and Uquía.

cards.q: Find Chilecito. What is it known for?
cards.a: Chilecito is La Rioja's wine capital and the core of the Famatina valleys, with about 580 ha of Malbec and much more Torrontés Riojano; La Riojana cooperative is based here, and the town still has the cableway built in 1904 to carry ore from the Famatina mines.

cards.q: Find Luján de Cuyo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Luján de Cuyo is Argentina's first denomination of origin and the historic home of fine Malbec. Key grapes: Malbec (8,920 ha of the department's 15,210 ha in 2024), Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Petit Verdot.

cards.q: Find Molinos. What is it known for?
cards.a: Molinos is a colonial village in the middle Calchaquí valley at about 2,000 m. Its department includes Colomé, founded in 1831 and one of Argentina's oldest working wineries, whose vineyards climb from 2,300 to 3,111 m, and the small high estate of Tacuil.

cards.q: Find Tunuyán. What is it known for?
cards.a: Tunuyán is the central Uco department, about 10,200 ha of vines (INV 2024), from the Tunuyán river plain to the Andean foothills.

cards.q: Find Cachi. What is it known for?
cards.a: Cachi, in the upper Calchaquí valley at about 2,300 to 3,000 m under the Nevado de Cachi, has about 117 ha of vines (INV 2024), 73% Malbec. Vineyards at Cachi Adentro and Payogasta are among the highest in the world.

cards.q: Find Tupungato. What is it known for?
cards.a: Tupungato is the northernmost Uco department, named after the 6,570-m Tupungato volcano that looms over it. About 10,600 ha of vines (INV 2024) climb from 900 m to over 1,500 m in Gualtallary.

cards.q: Find Tafí. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. Tafí (Tafí del Valle department) is Tucumán's wine IG, taking in Colalao del Valle and Amaicha del Valle on the Calchaquí side of the Aconquija range at about 1,700 to 2,000 m, where Malbec and Torrontés grow.

cards.q: Find Zonda. What is it known for?
cards.a: Zonda is the department west of San Juan city, in a valley between pre-cordillera ranges that gave its name to the Zonda wind. About 1,000 ha of vines (INV 2024) with a reputation for fresher Syrah and Malbec.

cards.q: Find Rivadavia. What is it known for?
cards.a: Rivadavia, in Eastern Mendoza along the Tunuyán river, has about 13,900 ha of vines (INV 2024). Nicola Catena planted his first Malbec here at La Libertad in 1902, and old-vine Bonarda from the East has become a cult value wine.

cards.q: Find Cafayate. What is it known for?
cards.a: Cafayate is the wine town of the Calchaquí valleys, at about 1,700 to 2,000 m, with roughly 2,765 ha of vines (INV 2024), three-quarters of Salta's total.

cards.q: Find San Martín. What is it known for?
cards.a: San Martín is the largest vineyard department in Argentina, about 25,800 ha in 2024 (INV), the heart of the Eastern Mendoza oasis along the Mendoza and Tunuyán rivers at 650 to 750 m.

cards.q: Find Los Chacayes. What is it known for?
cards.a: Los Chacayes is an alluvial fan at 1,100 to 1,600 m in western Tunuyán, recognised as an IG in 2017.

cards.q: Find Maipú. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. Maipú, east of Luján de Cuyo along the Mendoza river at 750 to 1,000 m, is the other half of Mendoza's historic Primera Zona.

cards.q: Find El Peral. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2022. El Peral is a district of Tupungato at about 1,100 to 1,300 m, recognised as an IG at the request of Bodegas Chandon. Chandon grows sparkling-base Chardonnay and Pinot Noir here; cool nights and stony soils also give fresh Malbec.

cards.q: Find Junín. What is it known for?
cards.a: Junín, in Eastern Mendoza, has about 10,800 ha of vines (INV 2024) and a reputation for generous Bonarda and Malbec from warm, sandy soils.

cards.q: Find La Consulta. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2014. La Consulta, a district of San Carlos at about 950 to 1,100 m, is old Malbec country: dozens of growers farm vineyards planted in the mid-20th century on deep alluvial soils.

cards.q: Find Agrelo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Agrelo, a district in southern Luján de Cuyo at 950 to 1,100 m, is one of the most planted fine-wine zones in Argentina and the home of Catena Zapata's pyramid winery and its La Pirámide vineyard (planted 1983). Key grapes: Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find Barrancas. What is it known for?
cards.a: Barrancas, in eastern Maipú on the banks of the Mendoza river, is a warm district of old vineyards known for ripe Malbec, Syrah and Bonarda. It was among the first Maipú districts registered as an IG, and among the most exported of small IGs in 2022.

cards.q: Find Vista Flores. What is it known for?
cards.a: Vista Flores is the Tunuyán district around which Michel Rolland and partners created Clos de los Siete from 1998: a block of about 850 ha divided among several wineries (Monteviejo, Cuvelier, DiamAndes, Rolland), each making its own wine and contributing to the shared Clos de los Siete blend.

cards.q: Find Las Compuertas. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2007. Las Compuertas, at about 1,050 m on the north side of Luján de Cuyo by the Mendoza river, holds some of Argentina's oldest Malbec vineyards, many planted in the early 20th century and still own-rooted.

cards.q: Find Vistalba. What is it known for?
cards.a: Vistalba, a small district at about 1,000 m beside Las Compuertas on the north bank of the Mendoza river, was recognised as an IG in 2022.

cards.q: Find Lunlunta. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2005. Lunlunta is a riverside district of Maipú, on high terraces above the Mendoza river at about 900 m. Old Malbec here, including Catena's Angélica vineyard planted in the 1920s, grows on stony alluvium and gives deep but fresh wines.

cards.q: Find Russel. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2005. Russell (registered as 'Russel') is a district of Maipú with deep soils and long-established vineyards for Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find Alto Agrelo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Alto Agrelo became Argentina's newest Luján de Cuyo IG in July 2025, at the request of Grupo Avinea, whose 232-ha organic estate there is the source of Argento's estate Malbecs.

cards.q: Find Gualtallary. What is it known for?
cards.a: Gualtallary, a district of Tupungato rising from about 1,200 to 1,600 m, is the closest thing Argentina has to a grand cru. Key grapes: Malbec, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find San Pablo. What is it known for?
cards.a: San Pablo, recognised in 2019, is Uco's highest IG, a cold alluvial terrace in Tunuyán at roughly 1,300 to 1,700 m, where frost and snow are real risks. Its limits were drawn by geology and climate rather than politics.

cards.q: Find Paraje Altamira. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2013. Paraje Altamira is the alluvial fan of the Tunuyán river in San Carlos, at about 1,000 to 1,150 m, and Argentina's most studied terroir. Key grapes: Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Semillon, Chardonnay.

cards.q: Find Pampa el Cepillo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Pampa El Cepillo, recognised in 2019, is the plain south of Paraje Altamira in San Carlos, around 1,000 to 1,100 m. It is cold, frost-prone and windswept, with stony, calcareous alluvium; Malbec and Cabernet Franc ripen slowly into firm, fresh wines.

cards.q: Find Cordón el Cepillo. What is it known for?
cards.a: Cordón del Cepillo, recognised in 2022, is a higher piedmont zone in San Carlos along the Cepillo range, west of Pampa El Cepillo. It is one of the newest Uco frontiers, with very stony soils and cool conditions.

cards.q: Find Valle del Tulum. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. The Tulum valley is the central irrigated oasis of San Juan around the provincial capital, at 600 to 700 m along the San Juan river.

cards.q: Find Valle del Pedernal. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2007. Pedernal is San Juan's high-altitude showcase: a narrow valley at about 1,250 to 1,500 m in Sarmiento department, between pre-cordillera ranges, where calcareous, stony soils and cold nights produce Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Chardonnay with real freshness.

cards.q: Find Barreal. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2013. Barreal, at about 1,650 m at the southern end of the Calingasta valley under the Mercedario peak, is one of the highest IGs in Cuyo. Cara Sur makes light, mountain Criolla and Bonarda here from old vines trained on parral.

cards.q: Find Valles del Famatina. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2004. The Famatina valleys, between the Famatina range (6,100 m) and the Velasco hills in La Rioja, are the province's wine heartland, with Chilecito at the centre at about 1,000 to 1,400 m. Key grapes: Torrontés Riojano, Malbec, Bonarda, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.q: Find Alto valle de Río Negro. What is it known for?
cards.a: Recognised 2002. The Alto Valle is the irrigated upper valley of the Río Negro from the Neuquén-Limay confluence east past General Roca, an apple-and-pear oasis at about 250 to 300 m.

cards.q: Find Trevelin. What is it known for?
cards.a: Trevelin, a town founded by Welsh settlers in the Andean foothills of Chubut at about 43°S, became an IG in 2020.

cards.q: Find El Hoyo. What is it known for?
cards.a: El Hoyo, a pre-Andean valley in the far north of Chubut near El Bolsón at only about 300 m, became an IG in September 2023 at the request of Patagonian Wines, the estate founded by Bernardo Weinert.

cards.q: Find Chapadmalal. What is it known for?
cards.a: Chapadmalal, on the Atlantic coast south of Mar del Plata, is Argentina's maritime wine experiment: Trapiche planted vineyards here around 2010 a few kilometres from the sea, and the IG followed in 2014.

cards.q: Name Argentina's two DOCs.
cards.a: Luján de Cuyo and San Rafael (Mendoza).

cards.q: Who brought Malbec to Mendoza, and when?
cards.a: French agronomist Michel Aimé Pouget, on 17 April 1853, now celebrated as World Malbec Day.

decks.title: Grape to region
decks.description: Name the classic regions for each major grape.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Cabernet Sauvignon.
cards.a: Pauillac, Margaux, Saint-Estèphe, Napa Valley. Blackcurrant, cedar, graphite and green capsicum; deep colour; high tannin and high acid; long finish.

cards.a: Pomerol, Saint-Emilion grand cru, Bolgheri, Napa Valley. Plum and fruitcake, chocolate and mocha from oak, round soft mid-palate, medium acid, medium+ but ripe tannin.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Cabernet Franc.
cards.a: Chinon, Bourgueil, Saumur-Champigny, Saint-Emilion grand cru. Raspberry and violet, leafy and graphite notes, medium body, high acid, moderate tannin.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Carmenère.
cards.a: Peumo, Valle de Colchagua, Valle del Maipo. Green pepper and jalapeño, black fruit, dark chocolate, soft tannin, moderate acid.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Malbec.
cards.a: Luján de Cuyo, Valle de Uco, Cafayate, Cahors. Inky purple, violet and blueberry, plush ripe tannin and medium acid (Argentina); rustic, tannic, earthy (Cahors).

cards.q: Name classic regions for Pinot Noir.
cards.a: Gevrey-Chambertin, Chambolle-Musigny, Vosne-Romanée, Pommard. Translucent pale ruby, high acid, low tannin, red cherry and raspberry, mushroom and forest floor with age.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Grenache.
cards.a: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Côtes du Rhône Villages. Pale for its weight; high alcohol, low acid, soft tannin; kirsch, strawberry jam, garrigue and white pepper; garnet early.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Mourvèdre.
cards.a: Bandol, Jumilla, Yecla, Barossa Valley. Gamey, meaty, earthy, black fruit and garrigue, high tannin.
cards.hint: Gamey, meaty, earthy, black fruit and garrigue, high tannin.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Nebbiolo.
cards.a: Barolo, Cannubi, Brunate, Vignarionda. Pale garnet with orange rim, very high tannin, high acid, high alcohol; tar and roses, sour cherry, liquorice; truffle and leather with age.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Sangiovese.
cards.a: Chianti Classico, Panzano, Radda, Castelnuovo Berardenga. Sour cherry, tomato leaf, dried herbs, leather; high acid, high tannin, medium body; ruby to garnet.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Barbera.
cards.a: Barbera d'Asti, Nizza, Barbera d'Alba, Barbera del Monferrato Superiore. Deep ruby with high acid and low tannin; cherry and plum.
cards.hint: Deep ruby with high acid and low tannin; cherry and plum.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Aglianico.
cards.a: Taurasi, Aglianico del Vulture, Aglianico del Taburno. Deep, very tannic and acidic; black fruit and smoke; the "Barolo of the south".
cards.hint: Deep, very tannic and acidic; black fruit and smoke; the "Barolo of the south".

cards.q: Name classic regions for Nerello Mascalese.
cards.a: Etna. Pale, high acid, firm tannin, red fruit and smoky ash; Etna.
cards.hint: Pale, high acid, firm tannin, red fruit and smoky ash; Etna.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Corvina.
cards.a: Valpolicella, Bardolino, Amarone della Valpolicella, Valpolicella Ripasso. Sour cherry and bitter almond (Valpolicella); raisin, chocolate and high alcohol (Amarone).
cards.hint: Sour cherry and bitter almond (Valpolicella); raisin, chocolate and high alcohol

cards.q: Name classic regions for Tempranillo.
cards.a: Rioja, Rioja Alavesa, Rioja Alta, Rioja Oriental. Medium acid, medium+ tannin; red to black fruit; leather, tobacco; coconut and dill from American oak (Rioja).

cards.q: Name classic regions for Mencía.
cards.a: Bierzo, Ribeira Sacra, Valdeorras, Dão. Violet and red fruit with herbs and slate minerality; medium body, fresh.
cards.hint: Violet and red fruit with herbs and slate minerality; medium body, fresh.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Touriga Nacional.
cards.a: Douro, Dão, Porto, Quinta de Vargellas. Violet and bergamot, black fruit, firm tannin, deep colour; Port and Douro.
cards.hint: Violet and bergamot, black fruit, firm tannin, deep colour; Port and Douro.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Baga.
cards.a: Bairrada. Very high acid and tannin, sour cherry and tar; Bairrada.
cards.hint: Very high acid and tannin, sour cherry and tar; Bairrada.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Zinfandel.
cards.a: Lodi, Dry Creek Valley, Sierra Foothills, Paso Robles. Jammy bramble fruit, raisin, sweet spice, very high alcohol.
cards.hint: Jammy bramble fruit, raisin, sweet spice, very high alcohol.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Pinotage.
cards.a: Stellenbosch, Swartland. Dark fruit, smoke, earth, banana and acetone; deep colour.
cards.hint: Dark fruit, smoke, earth, banana and acetone; deep colour.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Tannat.
cards.a: Madiran, Canelones. Very high tannin, deep colour, dark fruit and high acid.
cards.hint: Very high tannin, deep colour, dark fruit and high acid.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Xinomavro.
cards.a: Naoussa, Amyntaio, Goumenissa, Rapsani. Pale with very high acid and tannin; tomato, olive and sour cherry.
cards.hint: Pale with very high acid and tannin; tomato, olive and sour cherry.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Agiorgitiko.
cards.a: Nemea. Soft, plush cherry; Nemea.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Blaufränkisch.
cards.a: Mittelburgenland, Leithaberg, Eisenberg, Sopron. Dark cherry, pepper and spice with high acid; Kékfrankos, Lemberger.
cards.hint: Dark cherry, pepper and spice with high acid; Kékfrankos, Lemberger.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Zweigelt.
cards.a: Neusiedlersee, Carnuntum. Juicy cherry, soft, Austria's most planted red.
cards.hint: Juicy cherry, soft, Austria's most planted red.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Saperavi.
cards.a: Mukuzani, Kindzmarauli. Opaque teinturier with high acid; Georgia.
cards.hint: Opaque teinturier with high acid; Georgia.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Plavac Mali.
cards.a: Dingač, Postup. Ripe, high alcohol, firm tannin, dried fruit; Dalmatia; Zinfandel offspring.
cards.hint: Ripe, high alcohol, firm tannin, dried fruit; Dalmatia; Zinfandel offspring.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Sagrantino.
cards.a: Montefalco Sagrantino. Extreme tannin; dark fruit; Umbria.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Chardonnay.
cards.a: Chablis, Chablis Grand Cru, Petit Chablis, Meursault. A chameleon: high acid and citrus when cool (Chablis); butter, toast and stone fruit when oaked and warm. No marked aromatic profile of its own.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Sauvignon Blanc.
cards.a: Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé, Menetou-Salon, Marlborough. Pronounced gooseberry, grapefruit, passion fruit, cut grass and capsicum; high acid; light body; no oak.

cards.a: Hunter Valley, Pessac-Léognan, Margaret River, Sauternes. Lemon, grass and lanolin; waxy texture; toast and honey with age; the backbone of Sauternes.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Chenin Blanc.
cards.a: Savennières, Vouvray, Saumur, Swartland. High acid, apple and quince, wet wool and lanolin, honey with age; any sweetness level.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Riesling.
cards.a: Mosel, Saar, Wehlener Sonnenuhr, Scharzhofberg. Very high acid, aromatic (lime, green apple, peach, flowers), never oaky, from bone dry to luscious; petrol with age.
