cards.q: Name classic regions for Gewürztraminer.
cards.a: Alsace, Alsace grand cru Hengst, Alsace grand cru Furstentum, Alto Adige. Lychee, rose and ginger; low acid; full, oily body; high alcohol; deeper colour.
cards.hint: Lychee, rose and ginger; low acid; full, oily body; high alcohol; deeper colour.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Pinot Gris.
cards.a: delle Venezie, Alto Adige, Alsace, Willamette Valley. Grape with pink-grey skins: neutral and crisp as Grigio; pear, honey, smoke and spice, full and low-acid as Alsace Gris.
cards.hint: Grape with pink-grey skins: neutral and crisp as Grigio; pear, honey, smoke and

cards.q: Name classic regions for Viognier.
cards.a: Condrieu, Château-Grillet, Eden Valley, Virginia. Apricot, peach, honeysuckle; low acid; oily; high alcohol.
cards.hint: Apricot, peach, honeysuckle; low acid; oily; high alcohol.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Marsanne.
cards.a: Hermitage, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Péray, Nagambie Lakes. Full, oily, low acid, pear and almond, honey with age.
cards.hint: Full, oily, low acid, pear and almond, honey with age.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Grüner Veltliner.
cards.a: Weinviertel, Wachau, Wagram, Ried Achleiten. White pepper, green bean, lentil, citrus and green apple; high acid; no oak.
cards.hint: White pepper, green bean, lentil, citrus and green apple; high acid; no oak.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Albariño.
cards.a: Rías Baixas, Monção e Melgaço, Maldonado. Peach, citrus and saline sea spray; high acid; Galicia.
cards.hint: Peach, citrus and saline sea spray; high acid; Galicia.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Verdejo.
cards.a: Rueda. Herbal (fennel, bay), citrus, bitter almond finish.
cards.hint: Herbal (fennel, bay), citrus, bitter almond finish.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Godello.
cards.a: Valdeorras, Bierzo. Textured, mineral, pear and citrus; slate.
cards.hint: Textured, mineral, pear and citrus; slate.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Assyrtiko.
cards.a: Santorini, Dafnes. Very high acid with high alcohol; saline, smoky, citrus; Santorini.
cards.hint: Very high acid with high alcohol; saline, smoky, citrus; Santorini.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Furmint.
cards.a: Tokaj, Somlói, Podravje, Szent Tamás. Very high acid, smoke, quince and pear; Tokaj (dry and Aszú).
cards.hint: Very high acid, smoke, quince and pear; Tokaj (dry and Aszú).

cards.q: Name classic regions for Torrontés.
cards.a: Cafayate, La Rioja. Pronounced rose and jasmine, high alcohol, bitter finish; Argentina.
cards.hint: Pronounced rose and jasmine, high alcohol, bitter finish; Argentina.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Garganega.
cards.a: Soave, Soave Superiore, Recioto di Soave. Almond and chamomile, medium acid; Soave.
cards.hint: Almond and chamomile, medium acid; Soave.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Verdicchio.
cards.a: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi, Verdicchio di Matelica, Lugana. Green-tinged, high acid, bitter almond; Marche and Lugana.
cards.hint: Green-tinged, high acid, bitter almond; Marche and Lugana.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Fiano.
cards.a: Fiano di Avellino. Hazelnut, honey and pear; textured.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Greco.
cards.a: Greco di Tufo. Peach, almond, firm acid, mineral.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Cortese.
cards.a: Gavi. Crisp lemon and almond; Gavi.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Arneis.
cards.a: Roero. Pear and almond, soft acid; Roero.
cards.hint: Pear and almond, soft acid; Roero.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Carricante.
cards.a: Etna. Very high acid, citrus, saline; Etna Bianco.
cards.hint: Very high acid, citrus, saline; Etna Bianco.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Vermentino.
cards.a: Vermentino di Gallura, Colli di Luni, Patrimonio, Côtes de Provence. Citrus, herbs, saline, bitter almond finish; coastal Mediterranean.
cards.hint: Citrus, herbs, saline, bitter almond finish; coastal Mediterranean.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Melon de Bourgogne.
cards.a: Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, Clisson, Gorges, Le Pallet. Neutral, saline, tart, yeasty sur lie; light alcohol.
cards.hint: Neutral, saline, tart, yeasty sur lie; light alcohol.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Savagnin.
cards.a: Château-Chalon, Arbois, Côtes du Jura. High acid; vin jaune walnut and curry spice from voile; Château-Chalon.
cards.hint: High acid; vin jaune walnut and curry spice from voile; Château-Chalon.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Palomino.
cards.a: Jerez-Xérès-Sherry, Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda, Macharnudo, Miraflores. Neutral grape transformed by flor (bread, almond, saline) or oxidation (walnut, toffee); low acid.
cards.hint: Neutral grape transformed by flor (bread, almond, saline) or oxidation (walnut,

cards.q: Name classic regions for Pedro Ximénez.
cards.a: Montilla-Moriles, Jerez-Xérès-Sherry. Syrupy raisin, fig, date and coffee; very sweet; low acid.
cards.hint: Syrupy raisin, fig, date and coffee; very sweet; low acid.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Glera.
cards.a: Conegliano Valdobbiadene - Prosecco, Colli Asolani - Prosecco, Prosecco. Pear, green apple and flowers; light; tank-method Prosecco.
cards.hint: Pear, green apple and flowers; light; tank-method Prosecco.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains.
cards.a: Asti, Canelli, Alsace, Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise. Fresh grapes, orange blossom; from dry to sweet sparkling to fortified.
cards.hint: Fresh grapes, orange blossom; from dry to sweet sparkling to fortified.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Moschofilero.
cards.a: Mantinia. Rose and spice, light, crisp; Mantinia.
cards.hint: Rose and spice, light, crisp; Mantinia.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Petit Manseng.
cards.a: Jurançon, Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh, Virginia. Pineapple and spice with very high acid.
cards.hint: Pineapple and spice with very high acid.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Chasselas.
cards.a: Dézaley, Lavaux, Valais, Crépy. Neutral, soft, low acid; Swiss Fendant and Dézaley.
cards.hint: Neutral, soft, low acid; Swiss Fendant and Dézaley.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Trousseau.
cards.a: Arbois, Dão. Pale, red fruit and pepper, Jura red.
cards.hint: Pale, red fruit and pepper, Jura red.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Poulsard.
cards.a: Arbois. Almost rosé-pale Jura red.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Koshu.
cards.a: Yamanashi. Delicate, low alcohol, citrus; Japan.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Rkatsiteli.
cards.a: Tsinandali, Kakheti. Crisp, apple and quince; amber and tannic in qvevri.
cards.hint: Crisp, apple and quince; amber and tannic in qvevri.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Petite Arvine.
cards.a: Valais. Grapefruit, rhubarb, saline; Valais.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Sylvaner.
cards.a: Franken, Rheinhessen, Alsace grand cru Zotzenberg. Neutral, earthy, herbal; Franken Bocksbeutel.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Encruzado.
cards.a: Dão. Textured, mineral; Dão.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Arinto.
cards.a: Bucelas, Vinho Verde. Searing acid and lemon; Bucelas.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Loureiro.
cards.a: Lima. Floral, laurel, citrus, light; Vinho Verde.
cards.hint: Floral, laurel, citrus, light; Vinho Verde.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Sercial.
cards.a: Madeira, Jardim da Serra. Driest Madeira, very high acid, nutty, citrus peel.
cards.hint: Driest Madeira, very high acid, nutty, citrus peel.

cards.q: Name classic regions for Bual.
cards.a: Madeira. Medium-rich Madeira: caramel, raisin, high acid.
cards.hint: Medium-rich Madeira: caramel, raisin, high acid.

decks.title: Region to grape
decks.description: Find a classic region and name its signature grape and style markers.

cards.q: Find Pauillac. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Cabernet Sauvignon. Cassis, cedar and graphite on a firm, fine-grained frame; 12.5 to 14% abv; medium+ body; decades of ageing. The benchmark Left Bank blend, 60 to 90% Cabernet.

cards.q: Find Margaux. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Cabernet Sauvignon (also Petit Verdot). The most perfumed Médoc: violets, red and black fruit, finer and silkier tannin than Pauillac on thin gravel.

cards.q: Find Pomerol. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Merlot. Blue clay of the plateau: velvety, plush plum and black cherry, truffle with age, medium acid and fine, ripe tannin. Pétrus is about 100% Merlot.

cards.q: Find Saint-Emilion grand cru. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Merlot (also Cabernet Franc). Limestone plateau and côtes: fresher, more mineral Merlot blended with Cabernet Franc, firmer acid than Pomerol.

cards.q: Find Bordeaux. Which grape makes its classic rose wine?
cards.a: Merlot. Bordeaux rosé and clairet: deeper-coloured, fruity, Merlot-dominant.

cards.q: Find Chinon. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Cabernet Franc. Raspberry, violet and pencil lead with a leafy, gravelly crunch; tuffeau-limestone slopes give longer-lived wines than the river gravels.

cards.q: Find Bourgueil. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Cabernet Franc. Firmer and darker than Chinon, more tannin, from the gravel terraces and tuffeau slopes north of the Loire.

cards.q: Find Cabernet d'Anjou. Which grape makes its classic rose wine?
cards.a: Cabernet Franc. Off-dry to medium-dry, pink, raspberry-scented; must be at least 10 g/l sugar.

cards.q: Find Peumo. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Carmenère. The benchmark Carmenère site in Cachapoal: ripe black fruit and spice with less greenness; Concha y Toro Carmín de Peumo.

cards.q: Find Valle de Colchagua. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Carmenère. Warm Apalta and Colchagua: rich, ripe, oaky with chocolate and soft tannin.

cards.q: Find Luján de Cuyo. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Malbec. Classic first zone (900 to 1,100 m): plush, ripe, plum and chocolate, soft tannin.

cards.q: Find Valle de Uco. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Malbec (also Cabernet Franc). Higher (1,000 to 1,500 m+): brighter acid, violet perfume, chalky tannin, fresher blue fruit; Gualtallary and Paraje Altamira lead.

cards.q: Find Mendoza. Which grape makes its classic rose wine?
cards.a: Malbec. Fruity, deep-pink rosado.

cards.q: Find Gevrey-Chambertin. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Pinot Noir. Côte de Nuits power: darker cherry, more tannin and structure, earthy and gamey with age.

cards.q: Find Chambolle-Musigny. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Pinot Noir. The most perfumed and silky village: violets, raspberry and red cherry, lacy tannin on limestone-rich soils.

cards.q: Find Champagne. Which grape makes its classic sparkling wine?
cards.a: Pinot Noir (also Chardonnay, Meunier). Blanc de noirs and the backbone of most blends.

cards.q: Find Beaujolais. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Gamay. Light, juicy, pale purple, carbonic banana and bubblegum; Beaujolais Nouveau released third Thursday of November.

cards.q: Find Fleurie. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Gamay. Fragrant, floral (iris, violet), silky; pink granite.

cards.q: Find Touraine. Which grape makes its classic rose wine?
cards.a: Gamay. Touraine Gamay rosé and reds.

cards.q: Find Côte Rôtie. Which grape makes its classic cool and moderate climate wine?
cards.a: Syrah. The most perfumed: violet, raspberry and black olive, finer tannin; up to 20% Viognier co-fermented; Côte Brune (schist, iron-rich) firmer, Côte Blonde (granite, gneiss) softer.

cards.q: Find Hermitage. Which grape makes its classic cool and moderate climate wine?
cards.a: Syrah. Granite hill above Tain: the most powerful and long-lived, dense black fruit, meaty, high tannin; Bessards (granite) for structure, Méal (limestone pebbles) for richness.

cards.q: Find Barossa Valley. Which grape makes its classic warm climate wine?
cards.a: Syrah (also Grenache, Mourvèdre). Rich, ripe blackberry and plum, chocolate, mocha and liquorice; 14.5 to 15.5% abv; full body; soft, ripe acid (often adjusted); velvety tannin; Old Vine Charter ancestor vines (125+ years).

cards.q: Find McLaren Vale. Which grape makes its classic warm climate wine?
cards.a: Syrah (also Grenache). Mediterranean, maritime: ripe, rich, with dark chocolate, savoury herbs and a fresher finish.

cards.q: Find Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Grenache. Up to 13 permitted grapes, Grenache-led: kirsch, strawberry jam, garrigue, leather; 14.5 to 15.5% abv; full; soft acid; galets roulés on the La Crau plateau, sand at Rayas.

cards.q: Find Gigondas. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Grenache. Gigondas (min 50% Grenache): firmer, more rustic and higher-altitude, limestone of the Dentelles.

cards.q: Find Côtes de Provence. Which grape makes its classic rose wine?
cards.a: Grenache (also Cinsault, Tibouren). Very pale, dry, delicate: red berry, citrus and herbal; pressed directly.

cards.q: Find Tavel. Which grape makes its classic rose wine?
cards.a: Grenache (also Syrah). Tavel: rosé only; deeper, fuller, more vinous; maceration; Grenache-based.

cards.q: Find Bandol. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Mourvèdre. Bandol rouge (min 50% Mourvèdre): dense, gamey, black fruit, garrigue, firm tannin; long-lived; terraces (restanques) above the sea.

cards.q: Find Jumilla. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Mourvèdre. Monastrell: ripe, high alcohol, black fruit and liquorice, warm and soft.

cards.q: Find Barolo. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Nebbiolo. Pale garnet with orange rim even young; tar and roses, sour cherry, liquorice; very high tannin and acid; 14 to 15% abv; min 38 months ageing (18 in wood), riserva 62.

cards.q: Find Cannubi. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Nebbiolo. Barolo village: Cannubi mixes Tortonian (La Morra side) and Serravallian soils; perfumed and balanced.

cards.q: Find Chianti Classico. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Sangiovese. Sour cherry, violet, dried herbs and tomato leaf; high acid; firm, dusty tannin; galestro and alberese soils; Gran Selezione to be min 90% Sangiovese from 2027 vintage.

cards.q: Find Panzano. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Sangiovese. Conca d'Oro of Panzano: warm amphitheatre, rich and ripe.

cards.q: Find Barbera d'Asti. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Barbera. Barbera d'Asti: brighter, fresher, higher acid, red cherry.

cards.q: Find Nizza. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Barbera. Nizza DOCG (2014): 100% Barbera, riper, oaked, the top Asti tier.

cards.q: Find Taurasi. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Aglianico. Taurasi (Campania): volcanic, high tannin and acid, smoke and black cherry; min 3 years ageing (1 in wood).

cards.q: Find Aglianico del Vulture. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Aglianico. Basilicata, on the extinct Monte Vulture volcano: smoky, firm.

cards.q: Find Etna. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Nerello Mascalese. Etna Rosso (min 80% Nerello Mascalese): pale, high acid, firm tannin, red fruit and volcanic ash; contrade on the north slope (Passopisciaro, Solicchiata, Randazzo); 400 to 1,000 m.

cards.q: Find Valpolicella. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Corvina (also Rondinella). Valpolicella Classico: light, sour cherry, almond.

cards.q: Find Bardolino. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Corvina. Bardolino (and Chiaretto rosé): lighter still.

cards.q: Find Amarone della Valpolicella. Which grape makes its classic appassimento wine?
cards.a: Corvina. Grapes dried (appassimento) for about 3 to 4 months; dry or near-dry, 15 to 17% abv, raisin, dried cherry, chocolate, full body, high alcohol.

cards.q: Find Valpolicella Ripasso. Which grape makes its classic appassimento wine?
cards.a: Corvina. Ripasso: Valpolicella refermented on Amarone pomace, medium-full.

cards.q: Find Rioja. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Tempranillo (also Graciano). Rioja Gran Reserva: pale garnet, medium tannin, medium acid, dried red fruit, leather, tobacco, coconut and dill from American oak; long-aged before release.

cards.q: Find Bierzo. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Mencía. Bierzo: slate and schist slopes, fresh and floral with red fruit and herbs; vino de villa and paraje classification (Valtuille, Corullón).

cards.q: Find Ribeira Sacra. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Mencía. Ribeira Sacra: dizzyingly steep Sil and Miño terraces; light, mineral, perfumed.

cards.q: Find Douro. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Touriga Nacional (also Tempranillo). Douro DOC reds: floral (violet, bergamot), black fruit, schist, firm tannin.

cards.q: Find Dão. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Touriga Nacional (also Trousseau, Mencía, Alfrocheiro). Dão: granite, fresher, more elegant and long-lived.

cards.q: Find Porto. Which grape makes its classic vintage and ruby port wine?
cards.a: Touriga Nacional (also Touriga Franca, Tinta Barroca, Tinto Cão, Mourisco Tinto). Vintage Port: opaque, fortified to about 19 to 22% abv with aguardente (77% abv), 80 to 120 g/l sugar, very high tannin, black fruit and violets; decades of ageing; declared vintages only.

cards.q: Find Quinta de Vargellas. Which grape makes its classic vintage and ruby port wine?
cards.a: Touriga Nacional. Taylor's Vargellas: Douro Superior, floral, elegant single-quinta Vintage.

cards.q: Find Bairrada. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Baga. Bairrada: clay-limestone; very high acid and tannin, sour cherry, tar; ages for decades (Luís Pato, Filipa Pato).

cards.q: Find Dry Creek Valley. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Zinfandel. Dry Creek Valley: briary, spicy, balanced.

cards.q: Find Stellenbosch. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Pinotage (also Cabernet Sauvignon). Bush-vine Stellenbosch (Kanonkop): dark fruit, firm, smoky; Cape Blends require 30 to 70% Pinotage.

cards.q: Find Swartland. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Pinotage (also Syrah, Cinsault). Old-vine, fresher modern styles.

cards.q: Find Madiran. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Tannat. Very high tannin, dark fruit, firm, needs years; Montus and Bouscassé.

cards.q: Find Canelones. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Tannat. Uruguay's national grape: riper, rounder tannin, plum and raspberry, sometimes blended with Merlot or Pinot Noir.

cards.q: Find Naoussa. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Xinomavro. Naoussa PDO: pale, high acid and tannin, sour cherry, tomato and olive; the "Barolo of Greece".

cards.q: Find Amyntaio. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Xinomavro. Amyntaio: coolest Greek region, lighter, also rosé and sparkling.

cards.q: Find Nemea. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Agiorgitiko. Nemea PDO: soft, plush, cherry; valley-floor wines fruity, higher slopes (Koutsi, Asprokampos) more structured.

cards.q: Find Mittelburgenland. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Blaufränkisch. Mittelburgenland DAC: "Blaufränkischland", heavy clay, dark fruit.

cards.q: Find Leithaberg. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Blaufränkisch. Leithaberg: limestone and schist, tense, mineral.

cards.q: Find Neusiedlersee. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Zweigelt. Neusiedlersee DAC (Zweigelt): juicy, cherry, soft.

cards.q: Find Carnuntum. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Zweigelt. Carnuntum: Rubin Carnuntum, cherry-fruited.

cards.q: Find Mukuzani. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Saperavi. Mukuzani: dry, oak-aged Saperavi.

cards.q: Find Kindzmarauli. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Saperavi. Kindzmarauli: naturally semi-sweet.

cards.q: Find Dingač. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Plavac Mali. Dingač: steep south-facing Pelješac slopes over the sea, very ripe, high alcohol (often 15%+).

cards.q: Find Postup. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Plavac Mali. Postup: Croatia's second protected cru.

cards.q: Find Montefalco Sagrantino. Which grape makes its classic red wine?
cards.a: Sagrantino. Montefalco Sagrantino DOCG: among the most tannic wines in the world.

cards.q: Find Chablis. Which grape makes its classic unoaked cool climate wine?
cards.a: Chardonnay. Steely, high-acid, green apple, lemon and wet stone with a saline, oyster-shell edge on Kimmeridgian marl; 12 to 13% abv.

cards.q: Find Chablis Grand Cru. Which grape makes its classic unoaked cool climate wine?
cards.a: Chardonnay. Riper, broader and long-lived; seven climats on one southwest-facing slope; honey, smoke and iodine with age.

cards.q: Find Meursault. Which grape makes its classic barrel-fermented wine?
cards.a: Chardonnay. Rich, nutty, buttery and broad; hazelnut and toast; no grand crus but famous premiers (Perrières, Genevrières, Charmes).

cards.q: Find Puligny-Montrachet. Which grape makes its classic barrel-fermented wine?
cards.a: Chardonnay. Tighter, more mineral and floral than Meursault; citrus, white flowers and steely length.

cards.q: Find Sancerre. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Sauvignon Blanc. Restrained, mineral, citrus and green fruit with high acid; flinty silex (Chavignol is Kimmeridgian marl, Bué and Ménétréol caillottes and silex); 12.5 to 13% abv.

cards.q: Find Pouilly-Fumé. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Sauvignon Blanc. Across the river: smoky, flinty (silex) and slightly fuller than Sancerre.

cards.q: Find Sauternes. Which grape makes its classic sweet wine?
cards.a: Sauvignon Blanc. A minor partner (10 to 20%) giving acid and aroma in Sauternes.

cards.q: Find Hunter Valley. Which grape makes its classic unoaked, early-picked wine?
cards.a: Sémillon (also Verdelho). Picked early at 10 to 11.5% abv: light, lemon and grass, high acid; after 5 to 10 years in bottle develops toast, honey and lanolin without oak.

cards.q: Find Pessac-Léognan. Which grape makes its classic oaked blend wine?
cards.a: Sémillon. Blended white Graves (Haut-Brion, Domaine de Chevalier, Smith Haut Lafitte): citrus, wax and toasty oak, structured and long-lived.

cards.q: Find Margaret River. Which grape makes its classic oaked blend wine?
cards.a: Sémillon (also Chardonnay). SBS blends (Sémillon-Sauvignon), crisp and grassy.

cards.q: Find Savennières. Which grape makes its classic dry wine?
cards.a: Chenin Blanc. Bone-dry, austere, wax, quince and wet wool; needs 5 to 10 years; schist; Coulée de Serrant monopole.

cards.q: Find Vouvray. Which grape makes its classic dry wine?
cards.a: Chenin Blanc. Vouvray sec: apple, quince, chalk and honey with searing acid on tuffeau and silex.

cards.q: Find Montlouis-sur-Loire. Which grape makes its classic demi-sec and tendre wine?
cards.a: Chenin Blanc. Montlouis-sur-Loire, opposite Vouvray across the Loire, similar range.

cards.q: Find Mosel. Which grape makes its classic light, off-dry to medium-sweet wine?
cards.a: Riesling. Mosel Kabinett: 7.5 to 9% abv, off-dry to medium-sweet, green apple, white peach, flowers and slate, piercing acid.

cards.q: Find Saar. Which grape makes its classic light, off-dry to medium-sweet wine?
cards.a: Riesling. Saar: even more steely and racy.

cards.q: Find Clare Valley. Which grape makes its classic dry wine?
cards.a: Riesling. Bone dry, lime juice and lime blossom, high acid, 11.5 to 12.5% abv, toast and kerosene within 5 to 8 years; screwcap since 2000.

cards.q: Find Eden Valley. Which grape makes its classic dry wine?
cards.a: Riesling (also Viognier). Floral, lime, slightly more delicate than Clare.

cards.q: Find Alsace. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Gewürztraminer (also Auxerrois, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel, Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains). Alsace: pronounced lychee and rose, oily, full, 13.5 to 14.5% abv, often off-dry; vendanges tardives and SGN in warm grand crus.

cards.q: Find Alsace grand cru Hengst. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Gewürztraminer. Hengst: calcareous marl, powerful, spicy Gewurztraminer.

cards.q: Find delle Venezie. Which grape makes its classic light, crisp wine?
cards.a: Pinot Gris. Pinot Grigio delle Venezie: neutral, light, crisp.

cards.q: Find Alto Adige. Which grape makes its classic light, crisp wine?
cards.a: Pinot Gris (also Pinot Blanc, Gewürztraminer, Müller-Thurgau, Kerner). Alto Adige and Friuli Pinot Grigio: more concentration, still crisp.

cards.q: Find Willamette Valley. Which grape makes its classic rich, oily wine?
cards.a: Pinot Gris. Oregon Pinot Gris: medium-bodied, pear and spice, between Italy and Alsace.

cards.q: Find Condrieu. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Viognier. Condrieu: heady apricot, peach, honeysuckle and violets; full, oily; low acid; 13.5 to 14.5% abv; granite terraces; drink young.

cards.q: Find Château-Grillet. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Viognier. Château-Grillet: single-estate monopole (3.8 ha), more restrained, long-lived.

cards.q: Find Saint-Joseph. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Marsanne (also Roussanne). Saint-Joseph blanc.

cards.q: Find Weinviertel. Which grape makes its classic light wine?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner. Weinviertel DAC (first DAC, 2003; Grüner only): "Pfefferl", peppery, light, green apple and white pepper.

cards.q: Find Wachau. Which grape makes its classic light wine?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner (also Riesling). Federspiel (max 12.5% abv) and Steinfeder (max 11.5%): lighter Wachau styles.

cards.q: Find Ried Achleiten. Which grape makes its classic rich wine?
cards.a: Grüner Veltliner. Weissenkirchen Achleiten: gneiss and amphibolite, mineral.

cards.q: Find Rías Baixas. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Albariño. Rías Baixas: Val do Salnés (cool, coastal, saline), Condado do Tea (warmer, inland), O Rosal; peach, citrus and sea spray; pergola-trained on granite.

cards.q: Find Monção e Melgaço. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Albariño. Alvarinho in Monção e Melgaço: fuller, riper, 12.5 to 14% abv.

cards.q: Find Rueda. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Verdejo. Rueda: fennel, herbs, citrus and a bitter almond finish; night harvesting; often blended with Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: Find Valdeorras. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Godello. Valdeorras slate: textured, mineral, pear and citrus.

cards.q: Find Santorini. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Assyrtiko. Santorini PDO: kouloura basket-trained ungrafted vines on volcanic pumice (aspa); very high acid with high alcohol, salty, smoky, lemon; Nykteri (harvested at night, oaked).

cards.q: Find Dafnes. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Assyrtiko. Crete and mainland plantings: softer, fruitier.

cards.q: Find Tokaj. Which grape makes its classic dry wine?
cards.a: Furmint (also Hárslevelű). Dry Tokaji Furmint: high acid, smoky, quince and pear, full; single dűlő wines from Mád, Tállya, Tolcsva.

cards.q: Find Somlói. Which grape makes its classic dry wine?
cards.a: Furmint (also Juhfark). Somló volcanic butte: Furmint and Juhfark, smoky, salty.

cards.q: Find Szent Tamás. Which grape makes its classic tokaji aszú and eszencia wine?
cards.a: Furmint. Mád first growth: volcanic, structured Aszú.

cards.q: Find Cafayate. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Torrontés. Salta (Cafayate, Valles Calchaquíes) at 1,700 to 3,000 m: intensely floral, rose and jasmine, with a slightly bitter finish.

cards.q: Find Soave. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Garganega. Soave Classico on volcanic basalt (Monte Foscarino) and limestone: almond, chamomile, citrus; ages well; UGAs since 2019.

cards.q: Find Soave Superiore. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Garganega. Soave Superiore DOCG: lower yields.

cards.q: Find Recioto di Soave. Which grape makes its classic sweet wine?
cards.a: Garganega. Recioto di Soave: dried Garganega, sweet.

cards.q: Find Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Verdicchio. Castelli di Jesi: almond, citrus, saline, bitter almond finish; Riserva is DOCG.

cards.q: Find Verdicchio di Matelica. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Verdicchio. Matelica: higher, enclosed valley, more acid, more austere.

cards.q: Find Fiano di Avellino. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Fiano. Fiano di Avellino DOCG: hazelnut, honey, pear, smoky; ages well.

cards.q: Find Greco di Tufo. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Greco. Greco di Tufo DOCG: tuff and sulphur-rich soils; peach, almond, mineral, firm acid.

cards.q: Find Gavi. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Cortese. Gavi (Gavi di Gavi from the commune of Gavi): crisp, lemon, delicate, almond.

cards.q: Find Roero. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Arneis. Roero Arneis: pear, almond and flowers, soft acid, on sandy soil.

cards.q: Find Vermentino di Gallura. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Vermentino. Sardinia's only DOCG: granite, fuller, saline with a bitter almond finish.

cards.q: Find Colli di Luni. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Vermentino. Liguria and Tuscan coast: herbal, saline.

cards.q: Find Muscadet Sèvre et Maine. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Melon de Bourgogne. Muscadet sur lie (kept on its fine lees over winter and bottled straight off them): saline, lemon, yeasty, faint spritz; max 12% abv.

cards.q: Find Clisson. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Melon de Bourgogne. Cru communal Clisson: granite, long lees ageing (24 months minimum), riper and more complex.

cards.q: Find Château-Chalon. Which grape makes its classic vin jaune wine?
cards.a: Savagnin. Château-Chalon: vin jaune only, grey marl, the most intense; curry spice, walnut and green apple.

cards.q: Find Arbois. Which grape makes its classic vin jaune wine?
cards.a: Savagnin. Arbois vin jaune and sous voile whites.

cards.q: Find Jerez-Xérès-Sherry. Which grape makes its classic biological wine?
cards.a: Palomino (also Pedro Ximénez). Fino: pale, bone dry, 15 to 15.5% abv, bread dough, almond and chamomile from flor; Jerez and El Puerto de Santa María.

cards.q: Find Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda. Which grape makes its classic biological wine?
cards.a: Palomino. Manzanilla: Sanlúcar's coastal humidity keeps flor year-round; lighter, saline; Manzanilla Pasada is older.

cards.q: Find Montilla-Moriles. Which grape makes its classic fortified wine?
cards.a: Pedro Ximénez. Montilla-Moriles: PX often reaches 15% naturally; unfortified Finos too; PX sweet wines on albero.

cards.q: Find Conegliano Valdobbiadene - Prosecco. Which grape makes its classic sparkling wine?
cards.a: Glera. Conegliano Valdobbiadene DOCG: steep hills; Rive (single communes or hamlets) and Cartizze (107 ha); tank (Martinotti or Charmat) method.

cards.q: Find Colli Asolani - Prosecco. Which grape makes its classic sparkling wine?
cards.a: Glera. Asolo Prosecco DOCG.

cards.q: Find Asti. Which grape makes its classic moscato d'asti and asti wine?
cards.a: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains. Moscato d'Asti: frizzante, 4.5 to 6.5% abv, sweet, fresh grape; Asti spumante 6 to 9.5% abv, sweet; single tank fermentation (Asti method) stopped by chilling.

cards.q: Find Canelli. Which grape makes its classic moscato d'asti and asti wine?
cards.a: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains. Canelli DOCG: the hills around Canelli, the historic heart of Moscato.

cards.q: Find Mantinia. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Moschofilero. Mantinia PDO: high plateau (650 m), pink-skinned, rose and spice, light, crisp.

cards.q: Find Jurançon. Which grape makes its classic sweet wine?
cards.a: Petit Manseng. Passerillé (raisined on the vine): pineapple, mango and spice with searing acid, 50 to 120 g/l sugar balanced by high acid.

cards.q: Find Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh. Which grape makes its classic sweet wine?
cards.a: Petit Manseng. Late-harvest sweet whites from the Madiran zone.

cards.q: Find Dézaley. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Chasselas. Lavaux grand cru: richer, mineral, toasty and long-lived on steep lake terraces.

cards.q: Find Lavaux. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Chasselas. Lavaux UNESCO terraces over Lake Geneva.

cards.q: Find Yamanashi. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Koshu (also Delaware). Yamanashi: delicate, citrus, low alcohol, sur lie.

cards.q: Find Tsinandali. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Rkatsiteli. Tsinandali (with Mtsvane), European style.

cards.q: Find Kakheti. Which grape makes its classic orange wine?
cards.a: Rkatsiteli (also Mtsvane Kakhuri, Kisi). Kakhetian qvevri wine: amber, tannic, walnut and dried apricot; UNESCO 2013.

cards.q: Find Valais. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Petite Arvine (also Chasselas). Valais: grapefruit, rhubarb and a salty finish.

cards.q: Find Franken. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Sylvaner. Franken Silvaner in the flat Bocksbeutel: earthy, mineral, savoury on Muschelkalk (shell limestone); Würzburger Stein.

cards.q: Find Rheinhessen. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Sylvaner (also Müller-Thurgau, Souvignier Gris). Rheinhessen Silvaner: the largest plantings.

cards.q: Find Bucelas. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Arinto. Bucelas (min 75% Arinto): lemony, high acid, mineral.

cards.q: Find Vinho Verde. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Arinto. Pedernã in Vinho Verde.

cards.q: Find Lima. Which grape makes its classic white wine?
cards.a: Loureiro. Lima subregion of Vinho Verde: floral, laurel and citrus, light.

cards.q: Find Madeira. Which grape makes its classic fortified wine?
cards.a: Sercial (also Verdelho, Bual, Tinta Negra). Sercial: the driest (Seco) Madeira, searing acid, citrus peel and nuts.

cards.q: Find Jardim da Serra. Which grape makes its classic fortified wine?
cards.a: Sercial. High, cool vineyards for Sercial.

decks.title: Soils and the places they make
decks.description: From Kimmeridgian marl to Gimblett Gravels: which places sit on which rock.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Kimmeridgian marl?
cards.a: Chablis Grand Cru (Les Clos, Vaudésir); Sancerre (Chavignol, Les Monts Damnés); Les Riceys, Aube; Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Portlandian limestone?
cards.a: Petit Chablis plateau; Isle of Portland, Dorset.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Chalk?
cards.a: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Côte des Blancs; Cramant, Côte des Blancs; Nyetimber, West Sussex; Domaine Evremond, Chilham, Kent.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Jurassic limestone and marl (Côte d'Or)?
cards.a: Clos de Vougeot; Montrachet; Gevrey-Chambertin grand crus; Corton hill.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Tuffeau (Turonian limestone)?
cards.a: Vouvray; Saumur-Champigny; Chinon.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Galestro?
cards.a: Radda in Chianti; Gaiole in Chianti; Montalcino (northern slopes).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Alberese?
cards.a: Castellina in Chianti; Panzano (Conca d'Oro).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Tortonian and Serravallian marls (Langhe)?
cards.a: La Morra (Brunate, Cerequio); Serralunga d'Alba (Vigna Rionda, Francia); Barbaresco (Asili, Rabajà).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Terra rossa?
cards.a: Coonawarra, South Australia; Motovun, Istria; Kras (Karst) plateau.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Devonian slate (Mosel, Rhine and Ahr)?
cards.a: Wehlener Sonnenuhr; Ürziger Würzgarten; Bernkasteler Doctor; Ahr valley (Mayschoß).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Schist?
cards.a: Douro valley (Pinhão); Banyuls-sur-Mer; Côte-Rôtie, Côte Brune; Bannockburn, Central Otago.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Llicorella?
cards.a: Gratallops, Priorat; Porrera, Priorat.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Granite?
cards.a: Fleurie, Beaujolais; Hermitage (Les Bessards); Cornas; Swartland (Paardeberg).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Gneiss?
cards.a: Dürnstein, Wachau (Kellerberg); Spitz, Wachau (Singerriedel); Gorges, Muscadet.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Basalt and volcanic rock?
cards.a: Soave Classico (Monte Foscarino); Badacsony, Lake Balaton; Somló.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Volcanic ash and lava sands (Etna, Vesuvius, Campi Flegrei)?
cards.a: Passopisciaro, Etna; Campi Flegrei, Pozzuoli; Vesuvius (Boscotrecase).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Pumice and aspa (Santorini)?
cards.a: Pyrgos, Santorini; Megalochori, Santorini.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Picón (volcanic lapilli, Lanzarote)?
cards.a: La Geria, Lanzarote.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Tuff (volcanic tufa)?
cards.a: Tufo, Campania; Eger (Szépasszony-völgy); Pitigliano, Maremma.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Tokaj volcanic soils (rhyolite, andesite, zeolite, nyirok)?
cards.a: Mád (Szent Tamás, Úrágya); Tállya.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Kaiserstuhl volcanic rock and loess?
cards.a: Ihringen (Winklerberg); Achkarren (Schlossberg).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Loess?
cards.a: Wagram (Kirchberg); Kremstal (Krems); Rheinhessen hill country (Alzey).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Gravel (Médoc and Graves)?
cards.a: Pauillac (Lafite, Latour, Mouton); Margaux; Pessac (Haut-Brion).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Gimblett Gravels?
cards.a: Gimblett Gravels, Hawke's Bay.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Galets roulés?
cards.a: La Crau, Châteauneuf-du-Pape (Vieux Télégraphe); Château de Beaucastel, Courthézon; Lirac and Tavel.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Blue clay of Pomerol?
cards.a: Pétrus, Pomerol; Pomerol plateau.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Jory and Willakenzie (Willamette Valley)?
cards.a: Dundee Hills; Yamhill-Carlton; Eola-Amity Hills.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Missoula flood deposits?
cards.a: Red Mountain, Washington; The Rocks District, Milton-Freewater.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Albariza?
cards.a: Pago Macharnudo, Jerez; Sanlúcar de Barrameda (Miraflores).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Alluvial fans and benches?
cards.a: Rutherford Bench, Napa; Luján de Cuyo, Mendoza; Gualtallary, Uco Valley.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Sand?
cards.a: Colares (Azenhas do Mar); Château Rayas, Châteauneuf-du-Pape; Vin des Sables, Camargue.

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Caliche?
cards.a: Paso Robles (west side); Texas High Plains (Lubbock).

cards.q: Which wine places sit on Quartz, sandstone and kies (stony gravel)?
cards.a: Rüdesheimer Berg, Rheingau; Forst, Pfalz (Kirchenstück).

cards.q: Find Chablis Grand Cru. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Kimmeridgian marl. A grey limestone-marl laid down in a warm, shallow Jurassic sea about 157 to 152 million years ago, named after Kimmeridge in Dorset and packed with fossils of the small comma-shaped oyster Exogyra virgula.

cards.q: Find Petit Chablis. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Portlandian limestone. A hard, pale Jurassic limestone (now formally Tithonian), slightly younger than the Kimmeridgian, that caps the plateaus around Chablis.

cards.q: Find Côte des Blancs. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Chalk. A soft, white, very porous limestone made of the skeletons of coccoliths, microscopic algae that filled Cretaceous seas 70 to 100 million years ago.

cards.q: Find Clos de Vougeot. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Jurassic limestone and marl (Côte d'Or). The Côte d'Or is a fault scarp where Middle and Upper Jurassic limestones and marls are exposed in bands along a 50 km slope.

cards.q: Find Vouvray. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Tuffeau (Turonian limestone). A soft, fine-grained, cream-coloured Cretaceous limestone of the Turonian stage, found in the middle Loire around Saumur, Vouvray and Chinon.

cards.q: Find Radda. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Galestro. A crumbly, flaky schistous clay-marl that splits into thin, grey to reddish plates, common in the Chianti Classico hills and parts of Montalcino.

cards.q: Find Castellina. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Alberese. A hard, compact, pale grey limestone-marl of Eocene age found throughout Chianti Classico, especially Castellina, Castelnuovo Berardenga and the Conca d'Oro of Panzano.

cards.q: Find Barolo. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Tortonian and Serravallian marls (Langhe). Miocene marine sediments that form the Barolo and Barbaresco hills.

cards.q: Find Coonawarra. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Terra rossa. A red, clay-rich soil formed when limestone weathers and leaves behind insoluble residues coloured by iron oxides, typical of Mediterranean karst landscapes.

cards.q: Find Wehlener Sonnenuhr. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Devonian slate (Mosel, Rhine and Ahr). Slate formed about 400 million years ago when Devonian marine muds were compressed and folded.

cards.q: Find Douro. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Schist. A metamorphic rock formed when shale or mudstone is heated and squeezed, splitting into flaky layers.

cards.q: Find Priorat. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Llicorella. The Catalan name for Priorat's dark, crumbly slate and schist, glittering with mica and quartz, formed in the Carboniferous about 300 million years ago.

cards.q: Find Fleurie. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Granite. A coarse-grained igneous rock of quartz, feldspar and mica, which weathers into sandy, acidic, free-draining soils that are poor in nutrients (called gore in Beaujolais and arène elsewhere in France).

cards.q: Find Ried Kellerberg. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Gneiss. A banded metamorphic rock, formed from granite or sediment under great heat and pressure, with alternating light and dark mineral layers.

cards.q: Find Soave. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Basalt and volcanic rock. Basalt is a dark volcanic rock formed from fast-cooling lava, rich in iron, magnesium and calcium.

cards.q: Find Etna. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Volcanic ash and lava sands (Etna, Vesuvius, Campi Flegrei). Young volcanic soils formed from ash, lapilli, sand and broken lava, black to grey and rich in minerals but low in organic matter.

cards.q: Find Santorini. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Pumice and aspa (Santorini). Santorini's vineyards grow in aspa, a soil of pumice, ash and volcanic rock deposited by the Minoan eruption around 1600 BC.

cards.q: Find Lanzarote. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Picón (volcanic lapilli, Lanzarote). Black volcanic gravel (lapilli) blanketing much of Lanzarote after the Timanfaya eruptions of 1730 to 1736.

cards.q: Find Greco di Tufo. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Tuff (volcanic tufa). A soft rock of compacted volcanic ash, easily carved and porous enough to store water.

cards.q: Find Tokaj. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Tokaj volcanic soils (rhyolite, andesite, zeolite, nyirok). Tokaj's hills are volcanic, formed in the Miocene, with rhyolite, andesite and tuff weathered into clays such as nyirok (a red, sticky clay) and yellow loess on lower slopes.

cards.q: Find Kaiserstuhl. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Kaiserstuhl volcanic rock and loess. The Kaiserstuhl is a small extinct volcano in Baden's Upper Rhine plain, active in the Miocene, rising to about 557 metres.

cards.q: Find Wagram. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Loess. A yellowish, silty sediment blown by winds from glacial outwash during the ice ages.

cards.q: Find Pauillac. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Gravel (Médoc and Graves). Quaternary gravels and pebbles deposited by the ancestral Garonne and Dordogne, sorted into low ridges (croupes) along the Médoc and in Graves.

cards.q: Find Gimblett Gravels. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Gimblett Gravels. About 800 hectares of stony alluvium in Hawke's Bay, laid down by the Ngaruroro River, which changed course after a great flood in 1867, leaving a bed of greywacke gravels.

cards.q: Find Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Galets roulés. Large rounded quartzite stones, some as big as a fist or bigger, carried from the Alps by the ancestral Rhône and its glaciers and deposited on ancient river terraces.

cards.q: Find Pomerol. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Blue clay of Pomerol. A dense, dark blue-grey smectite clay of Eocene age, around 40 million years old, that comes to the surface on a small plateau at the heart of Pomerol, around Pétrus, in a formation called the 'boutonnière' (buttonhole).

cards.q: Find Dundee Hills. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Jory and Willakenzie (Willamette Valley). Oregon's Willamette Valley Pinot Noir grows on two contrasting soil families.

cards.q: Find The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Missoula flood deposits. At the end of the last ice age, between about 18,000 and 15,000 years ago, an ice dam holding back glacial Lake Missoula in Montana repeatedly burst, sending catastrophic floods across eastern Washington and northern Oregon.

cards.q: Find Macharnudo. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Albariza. A brilliant white soil of chalky marl, often over half calcium carbonate, rich in diatoms and radiolarians from the Oligocene and Miocene seabed.

cards.q: Find Rutherford. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Alluvial fans and benches. Fan-shaped deposits of gravel, sand and silt formed where streams leave mountains and spread onto valley floors.

cards.q: Find Colares. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Sand. Coarse, loose soils that drain fast, warm quickly and hold few nutrients.

cards.q: Find Paso Robles. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Caliche. A hardened layer of calcium carbonate that cements gravel, sand and clay together below the surface, formed when water evaporates in arid and semi-arid climates.

cards.q: Find Rüdesheimer Berg Schlossberg. Which soil or rock defines it?
cards.a: Quartz, sandstone and kies (stony gravel). Weathered quartzite and sandstone produce stony, acidic, free-draining soils.

decks.title: Wine law terms
decks.description: Quality tiers, label terms and sweetness scales around the world.

cards.q: What is meant by "PDO and PGI"?
cards.a: EU quality tiers since the 2008 to 2009 reform: PDO (AOP, DOP, DOC, DO, gU) needs 100% of grapes from the area and Vitis vinifera only; PGI (IGP, IGT, Landwein) needs 85% from the area and allows crosses.

cards.q: What is meant by "AOC hierarchy in Burgundy"?
cards.a: Regional (Bourgogne), village, premier cru (village name plus climat), grand cru (its own AOC, the climat name alone).

cards.q: What is meant by "Cru Bourgeois"?
cards.a: Médoc classification revived in 2020 with three tiers (Cru Bourgeois, Supérieur, Exceptionnel), revised every five years.

cards.q: What is meant by "Graves classification"?
cards.a: 1953, revised 1959: 16 châteaux classified for red and/or white, all now in Pessac-Léognan; no ranks within it.

cards.q: What is meant by "DOCG"?
cards.a: Italy's top tier: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, with government-numbered strip seals and a tasting panel; first awarded 1980.

cards.q: What is meant by "IGT"?
cards.a: Indicazione Geografica Tipica (1992): Italy's PGI tier, home of many Super Tuscans.

cards.q: What is meant by "Classico, Superiore, Riserva"?
cards.a: Classico: the historic core zone. Superiore: higher minimum alcohol or lower yield. Riserva: longer minimum ageing set by each disciplinare.

cards.q: What is meant by "Gran Selezione"?
cards.a: Chianti Classico top tier (2014): estate fruit, 30 months ageing; from the 2027 vintage min 90% Sangiovese and only native grapes.

cards.q: What is meant by "Spanish ageing terms (red)"?
cards.a: Crianza 24 months (6 in oak), Reserva 36 (12 in oak), Gran Reserva 60 (18 in oak) under national law; Rioja and Ribera set stricter oak minimums.

cards.q: What is meant by "Vino de Pago and DOCa"?
cards.a: Vino de Pago: single-estate PDO. DOCa (DOQ in Catalonia): Rioja (1991) and Priorat (2009) only.

cards.q: What is meant by "Prädikatswein"?
cards.a: German quality wine from must weight, without chaptalisation: Kabinett, Spätlese, Auslese, Beerenauslese, Eiswein, Trockenbeerenauslese.

cards.q: What is meant by "Grosses Gewächs"?
cards.a: Dry wine from a VDP Grosse Lage, released after a minimum period; the VDP pyramid is Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage, Grosse Lage.

cards.q: What is meant by "Trocken, halbtrocken, feinherb"?
cards.a: Trocken: up to 9 g/l sugar if acid is within 2 g/l of sugar. Halbtrocken: up to 18 g/l on the same formula. Feinherb is unregulated, roughly off-dry.

cards.q: What is meant by "DAC"?
cards.a: Districtus Austriae Controllatus: Austrian regional typicity appellation, 18 in all; Weinviertel first (2002 vintage).

cards.q: What is meant by "Puttonyos"?
cards.a: The old Tokaj measure of how many 20 to 25 kg hods of aszú berries went into a 136 l Gönc cask of base wine; since 2013 Aszú must have 120 g/l sugar and 5 or 6 puttonyos are optional labels.

cards.q: What is meant by "AVA"?
cards.a: American Viticultural Area: a TTB-defined grape-growing area based on geography; 85% of grapes from the AVA; no rules on grapes, yield or style. Augusta (Missouri) was the first in 1980.

cards.q: What is meant by "Varietal labelling in the US"?
cards.a: Federal rule: at least 75% of the named grape (Oregon requires 90% for most varieties); state of origin 75% (California 100%); vintage 85% (95% with an AVA).

cards.q: What is meant by "Wine of Origin"?
cards.a: South Africa's scheme since 1973: geographical unit, region, district, ward; single vineyard registered separately.

cards.q: What is meant by "Australian 85% rule"?
cards.a: Variety, vintage and GI claims each require at least 85% of the wine.

cards.q: What is meant by "VQA"?
cards.a: Vintners Quality Alliance: Ontario and British Columbia appellation system; Icewine must be from grapes naturally frozen on the vine, picked at -8 C or colder.

cards.q: What is meant by "Brut Nature to Doux"?
cards.a: EU sparkling sweetness terms: Brut Nature 0 to 3 g/l, Extra Brut 0 to 6, Brut under 12, Extra Dry 12 to 17, Sec 17 to 32, Demi-Sec 32 to 50, Doux over 50.

cards.q: What is meant by "Méthode traditionnelle versus tank method"?
cards.a: Traditional: second fermentation in the bottle with lees ageing (Champagne, Cava, Crémant). Tank (Charmat or Martinotti): second fermentation in a pressure tank (Prosecco).

cards.q: What is meant by "Vin doux naturel"?
cards.a: A French wine fortified during fermentation to keep natural sugar (Banyuls, Maury, Rivesaltes, Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise); min 15% abv.

cards.q: What is meant by "Vendanges tardives and SGN"?
cards.a: Alsace late-harvest and noble-rot wines from Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat, with minimum natural sugar levels.

decks.title: Wine history: put it in order
decks.description: Order the events of wine history; each card carries its year in "order".

cards.q: When: Grapevines domesticated in two places at once?
cards.a: c. 9000 BC. A 2023 study in Science, led by Yang Dong and Wei Chen with 89 co-authors, sequenced 3,525 wild and cultivated grapevines and concluded that grapes were domesticated about 11,000 years ago in two places at the same time: the South Caucasus, for wine, and western Asia (the Levant and Anatolia), for table grapes.

cards.q: When: Gadachrili Gora and Shulaveris Gora: the first grape wine?
cards.a: c. 6000 to 5800 BC. At two Neolithic villages of the Shulaveri-Shomu culture, about 50 km south of Tbilisi, archaeologists found pottery jars with tartaric acid and other grape markers.

cards.q: When: Areni-1: the oldest known winery?
cards.a: c. 4100 BC. In a cave above the Arpa river in Armenia, archaeologists led by Boris Gasparyan and Gregory Areshian uncovered a shallow clay treading floor sloping into a large jar, with grape seeds, pressed skins and drinking cups around it.

cards.q: When: Scorpion I's tomb: 700 jars of imported wine?
cards.a: c. 3150 BC. Tomb U-j at Abydos, built for a ruler of Upper Egypt known as Scorpion I, contained about 700 wine jars of roughly 6 litres each, stacked four rows deep in three chambers.

cards.q: When: Tutankhamun's labelled vintages?
cards.a: c. 1323 BC. Among the treasures in Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings were 26 wine jars with inscriptions recording the vintage year of his reign, the estate, the owner and the chief vintner, such as 'Year 5, sweet wine of the house of Aten, chief vintner Aperershop'.

cards.q: When: Thasos: the first wine-quality laws?
cards.a: c. 425 BC. Inscriptions from the island of Thasos in the northern Aegean record some of the earliest known wine regulations.

cards.q: When: The Opimian vintage?
cards.a: 121 BC. The year of the consul Lucius Opimius produced a legendary Roman vintage, remembered for generations.

cards.q: When: Vesuvius buries Pompeii's vineyards?
cards.a: AD 79. In late AD 79 (traditionally 24 August, though recent finds suggest October), Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii, a busy wine town whose amphorae were exported across the empire.

cards.q: When: Probus lifts the ban and plants the Rhine and Danube?
cards.a: AD 280. Emperor Probus, born in Sirmium in Pannonia, revoked Domitian's restrictions and, according to the Historia Augusta, allowed all Gauls, Spaniards and Britons to plant vines.

cards.q: When: Cistercians build the Clos de Vougeot?
cards.a: 1110 to 1336. Monks from Cîteaux Abbey, founded in 1098, received their first vineyard parcels at Vougeot in the early 12th century and gradually assembled about 50 hectares, enclosed by a stone wall by 1336.

cards.q: When: Eleanor of Aquitaine marries Henry Plantagenet?
cards.a: 1152. When Eleanor of Aquitaine married Henry, Count of Anjou, in 1152 and he became Henry II of England two years later, Bordeaux and Gascony came under the English crown for three centuries.

cards.q: When: Philip the Bold bans the 'disloyal Gamay'?
cards.a: 31 July 1395. Duke Philip the Bold of Burgundy ordered growers to uproot Gamay, which he called 'a very bad and disloyal plant', and to stop fertilising vineyards with manure, which raised yields at the expense of quality.

cards.q: When: First record of Riesling?
cards.a: 13 March 1435. An inventory of the cellars of Count John IV of Katzenelnbogen at Rüsselsheim on the Main records a purchase of 'seczlinge riesslingen in die wingarten', Riesling cuttings for the vineyard, for 22 shillings.

cards.q: When: Castillon ends English Bordeaux?
cards.a: 17 July 1453. French forces defeated the English at Castillon on the Dordogne, ending the Hundred Years' War and three centuries of English rule in Gascony.

cards.q: When: Tokaji Aszú is born?
cards.a: 1571 to 1631. Wines made from shrivelled, botrytised (aszú) grapes are recorded in Tokaj from at least 1571, and a 1576 dictionary by Balázs Fabricius Sziksai mentions them.

cards.q: When: Drake seizes 2,900 butts of sherry?
cards.a: 1587. In April 1587 Sir Francis Drake raided Cádiz, destroying Spanish ships and carrying off about 2,900 butts of 'sack', the fortified wine of Jerez.

cards.q: When: First wine in the Cape?
cards.a: 2 February 1659. Jan van Riebeeck, commander of the Dutch East India Company's Cape station, wrote in his diary on 2 February 1659: 'Today, praise be to God, wine was pressed for the first time from Cape grapes.' Vines had been planted in 1655 to help prevent scurvy among sailors.

cards.q: When: Christopher Merret describes sparkling wine?
cards.a: 17 December 1662. The English physician and scientist Christopher Merret presented a paper to the Royal Society describing how coopers and wine merchants added 'great quantities of sugar and molasses' to wine to make it 'drink brisk and sparkling'.

cards.q: When: Dom Pérignon at Hautvillers?
cards.a: 1668. The Benedictine monk Pierre Pérignon became cellarer of the Abbey of Hautvillers above Épernay in 1668 and held the post until his death in 1715.

cards.q: When: The Methuen Treaty?
cards.a: 27 December 1703. England and Portugal signed a commercial treaty negotiated by John Methuen: Portugal admitted English woollens, and England promised that Portuguese wines would never pay more than two thirds of the duty on French wines.

cards.q: When: Cosimo III delimits Chianti?
cards.a: 24 September 1716. Grand Duke Cosimo III de' Medici issued a decree defining the borders of four wine zones: Chianti, Pomino, Carmignano and Val d'Arno di Sopra, and set up a body to oversee production and fight fraud.

cards.q: When: Tokaj's royal decree?
cards.a: 1737. A decree of King Charles III of Hungary (Emperor Charles VI) defined the boundaries of the Tokaj wine region, listing the villages entitled to produce Tokaji.

cards.q: When: Pombal demarcates the Douro?
cards.a: 10 September 1756. After Port prices collapsed through overproduction and adulteration, Portugal's chief minister, the Marquis of Pombal, created the Companhia Geral da Agricultura das Vinhas do Alto Douro.

cards.q: When: The late courier of Schloss Johannisberg?
cards.a: 1775. Every year the monks of Schloss Johannisberg in the Rheingau had to wait for permission from their owner, the Prince-Abbot of Fulda, to begin the harvest.

cards.q: When: Veuve Clicquot invents the riddling table?
cards.a: 1816. Barbe-Nicole Ponsardin, widowed at 27 in 1805, took over her husband's Champagne house in Reims.

cards.q: When: James Busby's vine collection?
cards.a: 1832 to 1833. James Busby, a Scottish-born viticulturist who had taught in New South Wales, toured French and Spanish vineyards in 1831 and collected cuttings of about 650 varieties, which arrived in Sydney in 1832.

cards.q: When: Powdery mildew sweeps Europe?
cards.a: 1845 to 1857. In 1845 a gardener named Edward Tucker in Margate, Kent, noticed a white powder on greenhouse vines: oidium (powdery mildew, Erysiphe necator), a North American fungus.

cards.q: When: Pouget brings Malbec to Mendoza?
cards.a: 17 April 1853. Domingo Faustino Sarmiento, later president of Argentina, hired the French agronomist Michel Aimé Pouget to run a new agricultural school in Mendoza.

cards.q: When: The 1855 Bordeaux classification?
cards.a: 18 April 1855. For the Exposition Universelle in Paris, Napoleon III asked for a ranking of Bordeaux's best wines.

cards.q: When: Phylloxera arrives in France?
cards.a: 1863 to 1868. In 1863 vines began to die mysteriously in the Gard near Pujaut and Roquemaure, close to the Rhône.

cards.q: When: Pasteur explains fermentation and spoilage?
cards.a: 1863 to 1866. Asked by Napoleon III to investigate why French wines spoiled, Louis Pasteur studied wine in his native Arbois in the Jura and showed that fermentation was the work of living yeasts and that spoilage came from other microorganisms.

cards.q: When: Riley confirms the American origin?
cards.a: 1870 to 1871. Charles Valentine Riley, Missouri's state entomologist, showed that the leaf-galling insect on American vines was the same as the root-feeding aphid killing French vineyards, and that American vines tolerated it.

cards.q: When: Millardet invents Bordeaux mixture?
cards.a: 1882 to 1885. Downy mildew, another American import, reached France in 1878.

cards.q: When: Grafting rebuilds European viticulture?
cards.a: 1880s to 1900s. After years of failed remedies, including flooding vineyards and injecting carbon disulphide, French growers accepted grafting vinifera onto American rootstocks.

cards.q: When: France's anti-fraud law?
cards.a: 1 August 1905. With phylloxera-era fraud rampant, from wine made of raisins and sugar to cheap Algerian blends sold under famous names, France passed a law against fraud in the sale of goods, followed by a 1908 decree enabling the delimitation of wine regions.

cards.q: When: The Champagne riots?
cards.a: 1910 to 1911. Champagne growers in the Marne, ruined by poor harvests and phylloxera, rioted against houses buying cheap grapes from outside the region, including the Loire and the Aube.

cards.q: When: Prohibition in the United States?
cards.a: 17 January 1920 to 5 December 1933. The 18th Amendment and the Volstead Act banned the production and sale of alcoholic drinks.

cards.q: When: Châteauneuf-du-Pape writes its own rules?
cards.a: 1923. Baron Pierre Le Roy de Boiseaumarié, a lawyer and First World War pilot who had married into Château Fortia, persuaded Châteauneuf-du-Pape's growers to adopt strict rules: a delimited zone based on soils where lavender and thyme grew, permitted grape varieties, minimum alcohol, and a triage that discarded a share of the harvest.

cards.q: When: Perold creates Pinotage?
cards.a: 1925. Abraham Izak Perold, the first professor of viticulture at Stellenbosch University, crossed Pinot Noir with Cinsault (then known locally as Hermitage) at the Welgevallen experimental farm.

cards.q: When: France creates the AOC system?
cards.a: 30 July 1935. A decree-law created the Comité National des Appellations d'Origine, which became the INAO, empowered to define appellations by geography, grape varieties, yields, minimum alcohol and production methods.

cards.q: When: Burgundy's grand crus are named?
cards.a: 1936 to 1937. Following the 1935 law, the INAO created Burgundy's appellations between 1936 and 1937, including the grand crus of the Côte d'Or such as Chambertin, Musigny, Romanée-Conti, La Tâche, Corton and Montrachet.

cards.q: When: Max Schubert makes the first Grange?
cards.a: 1951. After visiting Bordeaux in 1950, Penfolds chief winemaker Max Schubert set out to make an Australian red that could age like a first growth.

cards.q: When: Italy's DOC law?
cards.a: 12 July 1963. Italy's Presidential Decree 930 of 1963 created the Denominazione di Origine Controllata system, modelled on the French AOC.

cards.q: When: Robert Mondavi opens his winery in Oakville?
cards.a: 1966. Robert Mondavi left the family's Charles Krug winery after a dispute with his brother and built a new winery in Oakville, the first major new winery in Napa since Prohibition.

cards.q: When: The Super Tuscans?
cards.a: 1968 to 1971. Marchese Mario Incisa della Rocchetta had made a Cabernet-based wine at Bolgheri for family use since the 1940s; Sassicaia's 1968 vintage, released in 1971, was its commercial debut.

cards.q: When: Germany's 1971 wine law?
cards.a: 1971. West Germany's new wine law classified quality wine by the sugar content of grapes at harvest (the Prädikat ladder from Kabinett to Trockenbeerenauslese) rather than by vineyard.

cards.q: When: Mouton Rothschild becomes a first growth?
cards.a: 21 June 1973. After a five-decade campaign, Baron Philippe de Rothschild won the only change to the 1855 classification's top tier: Château Mouton Rothschild was promoted from second to first growth by decree of Jacques Chirac, then minister of agriculture.

cards.q: When: The Judgment of Paris?
cards.a: 24 May 1976. Steven Spurrier, an English wine merchant in Paris, and Patricia Gallagher organised a blind tasting of California and French wines judged by nine French experts at the InterContinental hotel.

cards.q: When: Augusta becomes the first AVA?
cards.a: 20 June 1980. Regulations adopted in 1978 by the federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms created American Viticultural Areas, defined by geography rather than grape variety or method.

cards.q: When: Austria's antifreeze scandal?
cards.a: July 1985. Investigators found that some Austrian producers and merchants, mostly in Burgenland, had added diethylene glycol, a sweet compound used in some antifreeze, to make thin wines taste richer and sweeter, imitating late-harvest Prädikat wines.

cards.q: When: Cloudy Bay launches Marlborough Sauvignon?
cards.a: 1985. Montana had planted Marlborough's first commercial vineyard in 1973 and released a Sauvignon Blanc in 1980.

cards.q: When: Carmenère rediscovered in Chile?
cards.a: 1994. Visiting Chile, the French ampelographer Jean-Michel Boursiquot recognised that many vines grown as Merlot were in fact Carmenère, an old Bordeaux variety thought almost extinct.

cards.q: When: DNA reveals grape parents?
cards.a: 1997 to 1999. John Bowers and Carole Meredith at UC Davis used microsatellite DNA markers to show in 1997 that Cabernet Sauvignon is a cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.q: When: Clare Valley and New Zealand adopt screwcaps?
cards.a: 2000 to 2001. Frustrated by cork taint (TCA) and random oxidation, 13 Clare Valley Riesling producers bottled their 2000 vintage under screwcaps, and in 2001 New Zealand producers formed the New Zealand Screwcap Wine Seal Initiative.

cards.q: When: EU wine reform creates PDO and PGI?
cards.a: 2008 to 2009. The EU wine reform of 2008, applied from August 2009, replaced the old split between 'quality wine produced in a specified region' and table wine with two categories: Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) and Protected Geographical Indication (PGI), aligning wine with other agricultural products.

cards.q: When: UNESCO recognises qvevri winemaking?
cards.a: December 2013. UNESCO inscribed the 'ancient Georgian traditional qvevri wine-making method' on its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

cards.q: When: Burgundy's climats and Champagne join UNESCO?
cards.a: 4 July 2015. On the same day, UNESCO inscribed the Climats of Burgundy (1,247 named vineyard plots of the Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune) and the Champagne Hillsides, Houses and Cellars on the World Heritage List.

cards.q: When: The great April frost?
cards.a: 6 to 8 April 2021. After an unusually warm March pushed vines into early bud, temperatures fell as low as minus 6 degrees Celsius across France on three nights in early April.

cards.q: When: Germany reforms its wine law?
cards.a: 2021. Germany amended its wine law in 2021 to move from a ripeness-based system toward an origin-based pyramid, similar to France's: Gutswein (estate), Ortswein (village), Erste Lage and Grosse Lage at the top, with smaller origins having stricter rules.

cards.q: When: Science paper rewrites the domestication story?
cards.a: 3 March 2023. A team of 89 researchers led by Yang Dong of Yunnan Agricultural University and Wei Chen published in Science the largest genetic study of grapevines yet, based on 3,525 cultivated and wild samples.
